_readme: One source for provider support, evidence, and E2E test status. support states whether the cell is supported, or whether the agent or LeapMux sets the limit. userNote is the short note that the website shows. detailNote is the evidence for the maintainers, and the website never shows it. verified records the native support audit. testStatus records browser proof. The matrix validator that task validate-json runs requires one unique passing provider-feature spec for every cell.

supportStates.label: The agent does not offer it
LeapMux does not support it yet

providerGroups.userNote: Pi provides plan mode, session goals, to-do lists, agent questions and subagent tabs through extensions. The extensions come from the [Pi package catalog](https://pi.dev/packages): `pi-plan-mode`, `pi-goal-x`, `rpiv-todo`, `rpiv-ask-user-question` and `pi-subagents`. **Shift+Tab** does not toggle plan mode. Type the `/plan` command of the extension. Pi has native MCP support.
providerGroups.detailNote:
Pi extensions provide these features:
 - Plan mode and plan approval: [pi-plan-mode](https://pi.dev/packages/@narumitw/pi-plan-mode)
 - Session goal: [pi-goal-x](https://pi.dev/packages/pi-goal-x)
 - To-do list: [rpiv-todo](https://pi.dev/packages/@juicesharp/rpiv-todo)
 - Agent questions: [rpiv-ask-user-question](https://pi.dev/packages/@juicesharp/rpiv-ask-user-question)
 - Subagent tabs: [pi-subagents](https://pi.dev/packages/@tintinweb/pi-subagents)

 Pi's plan mode is a setting of the extension, not a setting of the provider, so **Shift+Tab** does not toggle it. Type the extension's `/plan` command to start planning.

Correction: Pi 1.0.0 (installed 2026-10-03) includes native MCP tools and resources, and its package ships an MCP guide. Pi needs no MCP extension. The dropped sentence was written for Pi 0.99.
providerGroups.label: Pi
Command Code
providerGroups.userNote: LeapMux drives Command Code through its experimental JSON-RPC mode and one official mod. This mode has no route for permission prompts, questions, plan approval, goals, or child agents. Command Code 1.74 and later also has an ACP (Agent Client Protocol) mode, which LeapMux does not use.
providerGroups.detailNote: LeapMux uses the installed native JSON-RPC transport and the official mod bridge.

providerGroups.label: DeepSeek Harness
providerGroups.userNote: LeapMux drives DeepSeek Harness through its Web Remote interface. LeapMux checked release 0.2.0-rc.2.
providerGroups.detailNote: LeapMux uses the native Web Remote transport for controls and session streams.

providerGroups.label: Gemini CLI
providerGroups.userNote: LeapMux tested Gemini CLI 0.62.0 over ACP. Gemini CLI links a subagent to its root session only, not to its direct parent. It offers no way to send input to a subagent or to cancel one.
providerGroups.detailNote: LeapMux uses installed Gemini CLI 0.62.0 ACP with exact native JSONL recovery. Native child UUIDs belong to the proven root session. Gemini supplies no direct nesting link or child input/cancel route.

providerGroups.userNote: LeapMux drives Muse Code 1.4.4 over its Muse Session Protocol (MSP). Children run inside workflow scripts (host.agent with submit_result) and carry no session of their own; the four approval modes include the bypass preset (allowAll) and no assisted preset.
providerGroups.detailNote: LeapMux uses the native MSP stdio host (muse serve). The private settings declare a config model catalog (context limits included) so the native model switch and the /compact summarizer both resolve under a local endpoint; a live MCP server in the shared settings would block the asynchronous compaction path, so the MCP spec registers its server per agent.
providerGroups.label: Muse Code

deepseek-harness.userNote: DeepSeek Harness saves an attached file and gives the model a handle. The model reads the content with a tool, so the content reaches the model one request later.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-file-attachments-probe: native upload saved exact file bytes. The model received its native handle. A real read or Bash byte read returned the complete content in the second model request. Each case made two requests with no unexpected request. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI reads the text of an attached file and sends it to the model.
gemini-cli.detailNote: Native ACP embedded context reaches Google contents[].parts[].text. The browser spec checks exact attachment bytes in the actual model request.

command-code.userNote: LeapMux sends an attached text file to Command Code as a text block, and the agent reads its contents.
command-code.detailNote: Native turn/start accepts text blocks. The installed RPC probe sends a text block and records it in the model request. LeapMux adds text attachments as native text blocks.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix 1.38.7 advertises no image input and ignores image blocks that arrive over the connection that LeapMux uses ([issue](https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/issues/8271)). LeapMux refuses images before the turn starts.
reasonix.detailNote:
Reasonix accepts text input on its ACP path. Its prompt converter drops image and binary blocks, so LeapMux refuses them before dispatch.

Classified as an agent limit: Reasonix 1.38.7 initialize returns promptCapabilities image false, audio false, embeddedContext true, and FlattenPrompt keeps text blocks and embedded text only. Reasonix 2.x (pull request #10920, merged 2026-09-26 on the studio branch; docs at v2.28.0) saves images and blob resources as attachments, so a retest with 2.x would make this a LeapMux limit (checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/issues/8271> (closed): The issue reports that Reasonix silently discards image resources in ACP mode and declares image false. It closed with pull request #10920.

zcode.userNote: ZCode accepts an image only on a model that declares image input. LeapMux refuses an image for any other model.
zcode.detailNote:
ZCode takes an image attachment only on a model that declares image input (see [Attachments](#attachments)).

This cell covers prompt attachments: LeapMux checks that the current model declares image input before it sends an image (checkZCodeImageSupport in providers/zcode/attachments.go). Pictures in tool results are a separate feature (images-in-tool-results).

deepseek-harness.userNote: DeepSeek Harness sends an attached image to the model as an image part with the exact bytes.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-image-input-probe: native image admission sends one actual image/png part with 168 bytes through Anthropic Messages. Its byte hash equals the existing valid 64x64 PNG fixture. One strict mock request, zero unexpected requests. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI sends an attached image to the model with its type and exact bytes. LeapMux also shows the image in the message.
gemini-cli.detailNote: Native ACP image input reaches Google inlineData with its MIME type and exact decoded bytes. The browser spec also checks the attachment bubble.

command-code.userNote: LeapMux sends an attached image to Command Code as image data, and the agent passes the exact bytes to the model.
command-code.detailNote: Native turn/start accepts base64 image blocks. Command Code converts each block to a data URI and sends it as a Chat Completions image_url part in the current user message, with the exact source bytes. The installed image probe records that request.

codex.userNote: Codex has no input type for PDF files, so LeapMux refuses them. [An upstream request for PDF support](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/1797) is open.
codex.detailNote:
Codex accepts text and image input blocks. Its LeapMux provider rejects PDF bytes because its native input has no PDF representation. See providers/codex/provider.go.

Classified as an agent limit: the Codex 0.160.0 app-server UserInput type has text, image, local image, audio, local audio, skill and mention entries, and no PDF or document entry. Upstream issue 1797 asks for PDF support and is open (checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/1797> (open): Asks Codex to read text, pictures, charts and tables of PDF files. No maintainer response, no linked change.

cursor.userNote: Cursor 2026.09.28 does not take PDF files over the connection that LeapMux uses. It replaces the PDF with its file name and a notice that it omitted the bytes. LeapMux refuses a PDF before the turn starts.
cursor.detailNote:
The installed Cursor CLI's ACP bridge replaces embedded PDF and binary resources with a filename and a notice that it omitted the bytes. LeapMux refuses these attachments before the turn.

Classified as an agent limit: the Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 ACP agent advertises embeddedContext false and replaces an embedded binary resource with its URI and the text '(binary content omitted)' (installed bundle read 2026-10-05).

github-copilot.userNote: GitHub documents PDF attachments for Copilot CLI on models that accept images. LeapMux does not send them yet. A LeapMux test with a custom model path showed only the file name reaching the model. See the [GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/overview).
github-copilot.detailNote:
The installed Copilot CLI sends a PDF as filename text on LeapMux's configured model path, even with Sonnet selected. PDF document blocks require an Anthropic provider that LeapMux does not configure. LeapMux refuses PDFs before the turn.

Classified as a LeapMux limit, with low confidence: the Copilot 1.0.87 SDK accepts blob attachments of any MIME type, and the GitHub documentation (checked 2026-10-05) states that Copilot CLI attaches images and PDFs on models that accept image input, on all plans. On the model path of the E2E mock, the CLI sends the PDF as file name text. That path is not the GitHub model path. A live check on the GitHub path needs a subscription token, and no LeapMux test uses a real subscription token.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/overview>: States: "You can attach images and PDFs to your prompts when using a model that supports image input." Lists JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, PDF, HEIC and HEIF. Available on all Copilot plans.

goose.userNote: Goose 1.53.0 accepts images and text files over the connection that LeapMux uses, but it drops an embedded PDF. LeapMux refuses a PDF before the turn starts.
goose.detailNote:
Goose converts ACP text resources and images. Its ACP bridge drops embedded blob resources, so LeapMux refuses PDF and other binary attachments before the turn starts.

Classified as an agent limit: Goose 1.53.0 convert_acp_prompt_to_message keeps text resources and images and ignores a blob resource, although initialize advertises embeddedContext true (source read 2026-10-05).

pi.userNote: Pi accepts text and images as input. It has no input type for PDF files, so LeapMux refuses them. See the [Pi RPC documentation](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc-commands.md).
pi.detailNote:
Pi RPC accepts text and image input. It provides no PDF or generic binary input path, so LeapMux refuses these files before dispatch.

Classified as an agent limit: the prompt, steer and follow_up commands of Pi 1.0.0 take a message and an images field in ImageContent format. They have no PDF or document field (documentation checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc-commands.md>: States that the prompt command takes images only, in the ImageContent format (base64 data and MIME type). No PDF or other binary field.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix 1.38.7 reads only text over the connection that LeapMux uses. It drops a PDF ([issue](https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/issues/8271)), so LeapMux refuses a PDF before the turn starts.
reasonix.detailNote:
Reasonix accepts text input on its ACP path. Its prompt converter drops image and binary blocks, so LeapMux refuses them before dispatch.

Classified as an agent limit: Reasonix 1.38.7 FlattenPrompt keeps text blocks and the text of embedded resources, and drops every other block (source and documentation read 2026-10-05). Reasonix 2.x saves blob resources as attachments (pull request #10920), so a retest with 2.x would make this a LeapMux limit.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/issues/8271> (closed): The issue reports that Reasonix silently discards embedded resource content in ACP mode. It closed with pull request #10920.

zcode.userNote: ZCode accepts a PDF file on a model that declares PDF input. LeapMux does not send PDF files to ZCode yet, so it refuses them.
zcode.detailNote:
LeapMux sends text and supported images to ZCode.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: ZCode 3.14.4 (engine 0.16.9) maps a send attachment of kind pdf, or of media type application/pdf, to a pdf turn attachment (function GYa in zcode.cjs). The engine then checks the model for PDF input (supportsPdf). The comment in providers/zcode/attachments.go, which says that a PDF has no kind of its own, does not match this build (checked 2026-10-05). The native prompt path carries a PDF, so the limit is in LeapMux: LeapMux refuses the file because it does not send it yet.

codewhale.userNote: CodeWhale's runtime accepts only text and inline images in a message, so LeapMux cannot send a PDF file to CodeWhale. LeapMux refuses the attachment.
codewhale.detailNote:
The current Codewhale attachment path refuses PDF bytes. It supplies no supported native PDF input in LeapMux.

Classified as an agent limit: the turn body of CodeWhale 0.10.0 holds `images: [{mime, dataBase64}]` and no file field; an `@path` in the prompt is only a convention. CodeWhale's own `read_file` tool extracts PDF text by path when the optional `pdftotext` program exists; using it would need LeapMux to write the file and name its path, which is an emulation that LeapMux does not build (documentation and source checked 2026-10-05).

kimi-code.userNote: Kimi Code cannot read a PDF file. Its file tool refuses PDFs, and its media tool reads only images and videos, so LeapMux refuses a PDF attachment. See [Kimi Code's tools reference](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/reference/tools.html).
kimi-code.detailNote:
The current Kimi Code attachment path refuses PDF bytes. It supplies no supported native PDF input in LeapMux.

Classified as an agent limit: a `file` part of Kimi Code 2.1.1 only adds a text notice with the file path, and the `Read` tool answers 'not readable' for a PDF, while `ReadMediaFile` accepts images and videos (source checked 2026-10-05). The model would need Bash or an MCP tool to read the file, which is an emulation that LeapMux does not build.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/reference/tools.html>: ReadMediaFile sends an image or video to the model; the page lists no tool that reads a PDF.

oh-my-pi.userNote: Oh My Pi accepts text and images as input. It has no input type for PDF files, so LeapMux refuses them. See the [Oh My Pi RPC documentation](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/rpc.md).
oh-my-pi.detailNote:
The current Oh My Pi attachment path refuses PDF bytes. It supplies no supported native PDF input in LeapMux.

Classified as an agent limit: the prompt, steer and follow_up commands of Oh My Pi 18.6.0 take a message and an images field (ImageContent[]), and its wire user content type is text or image. It has no PDF or document field (documentation checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/rpc.md>: The prompt command schema takes message and images (ImageContent[]). The wire content type is text or image only.

amp.userNote: Amp's stream input accepts only text and images, so LeapMux cannot send a PDF file to Amp. LeapMux refuses the attachment. See [Amp's streaming JSON documentation](https://ampcode.com/docs/cli/streaming-json).
amp.detailNote:
The current Amp attachment path refuses PDF bytes. It supplies no supported native PDF input in LeapMux.

Classified as an agent limit: the stdin schema of Amp 0.0.1791074829 stream-JSON takes text blocks and base64 image blocks (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) only; the installed CLI bundle rejects any other block (checked 2026-10-05). The `--attach` flag uploads files only with a remote executor (`-ox`), and a remote executor refuses `--stream-json-input`. Writing the file to disk and telling the model its path would be an emulation that LeapMux does not build.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://ampcode.com/docs/cli/streaming-json>: The stream JSON input schema lists text blocks and image blocks (jpeg, png, gif, webp) only.

cline.userNote: Cline's input accepts only text files and images, so LeapMux cannot send a PDF file to Cline. LeapMux refuses the attachment.
cline.detailNote:
The current Cline attachment path refuses PDF bytes. It supplies no supported native PDF input in LeapMux.

Classified as an agent limit: the hub command `session.send_input` of Cline 3.0.68 takes `userImages` (data URLs) and `userFiles` (paths that the daemon reads as text); the SDK builds no PDF block for a user message (source checked 2026-10-05). Cline's VS Code extension extracts PDF text in its own client code, outside the hub; LeapMux would need to build that emulation. Medium confidence because the Cline documentation says drag and drop accepts PDFs in that extension.

junie.userNote: Junie documents image input only, so LeapMux refuses a PDF file. See the [Junie docs](https://junie.jetbrains.com/docs/junie-cli.html).
junie.detailNote:
Junie exposes no supported PDF input through this integration. LeapMux refuses the upload and keeps the actual file bytes out of the next native model request.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: the Junie 26.9.22 docs state image inputs only (PNG and JPEG). Its ACP prompt capabilities are image true, audio false, and embeddedContext true. AcpPromptAttachmentStorage writes an inline blob to a temporary file (acp-prompt-attachments), and Junie has no PDF reader. LeapMux refuses the upload in junieProvider.ValidateAttachment, so the agent was not tried with a PDF (checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://junie.jetbrains.com/docs/junie-cli.html>: The quickstart documents image inputs (PNG and JPEG) and the @ file reference. It does not mention PDF or other file attachments.

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code accepts only text and images in a message. It has no input for PDF files, so LeapMux refuses a PDF upload for it.
letta-code.detailNote:
Letta Code exposes no supported PDF input through this integration. LeapMux refuses the upload and keeps the actual file bytes out of the next native model request.

Classified as an agent limit: Letta Code 0.34.2 accepts text parts and base64 image parts in a message (installed letta.js checked 2026-10-05).

dirac.userNote: Dirac reads only the text and images of a message. It drops the bytes of a PDF, so LeapMux refuses to attach one.
dirac.detailNote:
Dirac exposes no supported PDF input through this integration. LeapMux refuses the upload and keeps the actual file bytes out of the next native model request.

Classified as an agent limit. Dirac 0.5.17 parsePromptContent keeps text blocks, image blocks and only the URI of an embedded resource. PDF bytes never reach the model (upstream source checked 2026-10-05). Dirac extracts PDF text only from a file path on the host. LeapMux does not build that route.

qoder-cli.userNote: Qoder CLI reads only text and image blocks in its stream JSON input. It cannot represent a PDF block as model input, so LeapMux refuses a PDF upload for it.
qoder-cli.detailNote:
Qoder's prompt parser ignores inline PDF and binary blocks. Its file-upload path requires a separate file identifier that LeapMux does not create.

Classified as an agent limit: the stream JSON input of Qoder CLI 1.1.65 carries text and image blocks only (installed binary strings checked 2026-10-05). The documentation lists PDF as multimodal input, and the --attachment flag attaches files to the initial prompt only, so a long-lived stream session cannot use it. A model that reads a PDF by path would be an emulation that LeapMux does not build.

factory-droid.userNote: Factory Droid accepts a PDF file as message input, but LeapMux does not send PDF files to it yet. LeapMux refuses a PDF upload for this agent.
factory-droid.detailNote:
LeapMux refuses the upload and keeps the actual file bytes out of the next native model request.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the droid.add_user_message schema of Droid 0.233.0 has a files input for base64 application/pdf documents. LeapMux sends only images and inline text (installed binary strings checked 2026-10-05). Droid accepts a PDF in the files input, and only LeapMux refuses it. Not run natively: a model without PDF support may need parsedData text that the client extracts.

fast-agent.userNote: Fast Agent takes a PDF from the composer as an embedded document. LeapMux sends no other binary file to Fast Agent.
fast-agent.detailNote: Fast Agent receives a composer PDF as an ACP embedded resource. Its `attach_media` tool stages media through a separate path. Fast Agent sends image blocks in ACP tool results, but it does not accept a generic binary composer attachment.

deepseek-harness.userNote: DeepSeek Harness saves an attached PDF file and gives the model a handle. The model reads the bytes with a tool, so the content reaches the model one request later.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-file-attachments-probe: native upload saved exact file bytes. The model received its native handle. A real read or Bash byte read returned the complete content in the second model request. Each case made two requests with no unexpected request. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI sends an attached PDF to the model as a PDF document, not only as a file name.
gemini-cli.detailNote: Native ACP PDF input reaches Google inlineData as application/pdf. The browser spec checks exact decoded bytes, rather than the filename alone.

command-code.userNote: Command Code's JSON-RPC mode accepts only text and images, so LeapMux cannot send it a PDF file. LeapMux refuses the attachment.
command-code.detailNote:
The native RPC parseBlock accepts text and base64 images only. It rejects document blocks. Native file conversion is separate from direct attachments.

Classified as an agent limit: parseBlock in Command Code 1.74.1 (dist/cli.mjs, checked 2026-10-05) throws invalid params for any block that is not a text block or a base64 image block. LeapMux rejects the attachment before it sends the turn.

muse-code.userNote: Muse MSP input accepts text and images only; its media/upload route carries video alone. LeapMux refuses PDF attachments.
muse-code.detailNote: Muse MSP input accepts text and images only; its media/upload route carries video alone. LeapMux refuses PDF attachments. The deciding evidence came from the binary itself: its exported MSP schema and a live muse serve probe under the local mock.

claude-code.userNote: Claude Code accepts text, images and PDF documents as input. It has no input type for other binary files, so LeapMux refuses them. See the [Claude API documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support).
claude-code.detailNote:
LeapMux rejects binary attachments for Claude Code. The native message input supports text, images, and PDF documents, without a general binary block.

Classified as an agent limit: Claude Code 2.1.289 reads user input as text, image and document blocks. The Claude API documentation (checked 2026-10-05) states that binary formats such as .xlsx and .docx are not supported in document blocks.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support>: States that plain text files work in document blocks and that binary formats such as .xlsx or .docx are not supported in document blocks.

codex.userNote: Codex 0.160.0 accepts audio on models that list audio input, and LeapMux does not send it yet. Codex has no input type for any other binary file, so LeapMux refuses every binary file.
codex.detailNote:
Codex accepts text and image input blocks. Its LeapMux provider rejects other binary bytes because its native input has no general binary representation. See providers/codex/provider.go.

Classified as a LeapMux limit, because the native protocol carries part of the feature. The Codex 0.160.0 UserInput type carries audio as a data URI or as a local path (wav, mp3, m4a, webm and ogg). It has no general binary entry (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/protocol/src/user_input.rs, fetched 2026-10-05). Audio needs a model whose input modalities include audio. LeapMux refuses every non-image binary file, so it refuses audio. The spec asserts the refusal of a generic binary file, which Codex cannot carry, so the audit value stays unsupported.

cursor.userNote: Cursor 2026.09.28 does not take binary files over the connection that LeapMux uses. It replaces a binary file with its file name and a notice that it omitted the bytes. LeapMux refuses a binary file before the turn starts.
cursor.detailNote:
The installed Cursor CLI's ACP bridge replaces embedded PDF and binary resources with a filename and a notice that it omitted the bytes. LeapMux refuses these attachments before the turn.

Classified as an agent limit: the Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 ACP agent advertises embeddedContext false and replaces an embedded binary resource with its URI and the text '(binary content omitted)' (installed bundle read 2026-10-05).

github-copilot.userNote: Copilot CLI documents attachments for images and PDFs only. A binary file reaches the CLI, but the model receives only its file name, so LeapMux refuses it. See the [GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/overview).
github-copilot.detailNote:
On LeapMux's current GitHub Copilot model path, a generic binary blob reaches the CLI but only its filename reaches the model. LeapMux refuses the blob before the turn.

Classified as an agent limit: the GitHub documentation (checked 2026-10-05) lists image and PDF formats only. The 1.0.87 SDK accepts a blob of any type, and a probe showed that only the file name of a generic binary reached the model.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/overview>: Lists the attachable formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, PDF, HEIC, HEIF.

kilo.userNote: Kilo 7.8.1 cannot send a generic binary file to its model. The model adapter rejects the file type, so LeapMux refuses the file before the turn starts.
kilo.detailNote:
OpenCode and Kilo accept an ACP binary resource, but their configured model adapter rejects its `application/octet-stream` file part. LeapMux refuses that attachment before the turn starts.

Classified as an agent limit: Kilo 7.8.1 keeps the OpenCode file part path and the same mimeToModality mapping (provider/transform.ts at tag v7.8.1), so a generic binary file reaches the model adapter, which rejects it. The same rejection is reported for OpenCode (anomalyco/opencode#38794).

opencode.userNote: OpenCode 1.18.34 cannot send a generic binary file to its model. The model adapter rejects the file type ([upstream report](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/38794)), so LeapMux refuses the file before the turn starts.
opencode.detailNote:
OpenCode and Kilo accept an ACP binary resource, but their configured model adapter rejects its `application/octet-stream` file part. LeapMux refuses that attachment before the turn starts.

Classified as an agent limit: OpenCode 1.18.34 builds a model file part from any attached type (session/message-v2.ts), but provider/transform.ts maps only image, audio, video, and PDF types to an input kind. The model adapter (@ai-sdk/openai-compatible) throws a media type error for application/octet-stream (checked 2026-10-05; upstream report anomalyco/opencode#38794).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/38794> (closed): A user of OpenCode 1.18.4 reports the error 'file part media type application/octet-stream functionality not supported'. The issue closed as not planned.

goose.userNote: Goose 1.53.0 accepts images and text files over the connection that LeapMux uses, but it drops an embedded binary file. LeapMux refuses a binary file before the turn starts.
goose.detailNote:
Goose converts ACP text resources and images. Its ACP bridge drops embedded blob resources, so LeapMux refuses PDF and other binary attachments before the turn starts.

Classified as an agent limit: Goose 1.53.0 convert_acp_prompt_to_message keeps text resources and images and ignores a blob resource, although initialize advertises embeddedContext true (source read 2026-10-05).

pi.userNote: Pi accepts text and images as input. It has no input type for binary files other than images, so LeapMux refuses them. See the [Pi RPC documentation](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc-commands.md).
pi.detailNote:
Pi RPC accepts text and image input. It provides no PDF or generic binary input path, so LeapMux refuses these files before dispatch.

Classified as an agent limit: the prompt, steer and follow_up commands of Pi 1.0.0 take a message and an images field in ImageContent format. They have no field for other binary data (documentation checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc-commands.md>: States that the prompt command takes images only, in the ImageContent format (base64 data and MIME type). No PDF or other binary field.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix 1.38.7 reads only text over the connection that LeapMux uses. It drops a binary file ([issue](https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/issues/8271)), so LeapMux refuses a binary file before the turn starts.
reasonix.detailNote:
Reasonix accepts text input on its ACP path. Its prompt converter drops image and binary blocks, so LeapMux refuses them before dispatch.

Classified as an agent limit: Reasonix 1.38.7 FlattenPrompt keeps text blocks and the text of embedded resources, and drops every other block (source and documentation read 2026-10-05). Reasonix 2.x saves blob resources as attachments (pull request #10920), so a retest with 2.x would make this a LeapMux limit.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/issues/8271> (closed): The issue reports that Reasonix silently discards embedded resource content in ACP mode. It closed with pull request #10920.

zcode.userNote: ZCode 3.14.4 cannot use the bytes of a generic binary file. It decodes a small file as text and drops a large one, so LeapMux refuses the file.
zcode.detailNote:
LeapMux sends text and supported images to ZCode.

Classified as an agent limit: the ZCode 3.14.4 normalizer (GYa in zcode.cjs) keeps a file attachment as a path, as given text, or as UTF-8 text decoded from at most 64 KiB of bytes. It drops a larger file. Only image, video, and PDF attachments keep their bytes (checked 2026-10-05). The native prompt path carries a PDF (see pdf-attachments of zcode), but it carries no generic binary input, so this limit stands.

codewhale.userNote: CodeWhale's runtime accepts only text and inline images in a message. Its file tool cannot read other binary files, so LeapMux refuses a binary attachment.
codewhale.detailNote:
The current Codewhale attachment path refuses arbitrary binary bytes. It does not convert a filename into usable binary input.

Classified as an agent limit: the turn body of CodeWhale 0.10.0 has no file field, and the description of its `read_file` tool says that it cannot read binary files other than PDFs (documentation and source checked 2026-10-05).

kimi-code.userNote: Kimi Code can read only text files, images, and videos. Its tools refuse other binary files, so LeapMux refuses a binary attachment.
kimi-code.detailNote:
The current Kimi Code attachment path refuses arbitrary binary bytes. It does not convert a filename into usable binary input.

Classified as an agent limit: Kimi Code 2.1.1 gives the model only a path notice for a `file` part, and `Read` and `ReadMediaFile` refuse other binary formats; the media tool says to use Bash or an MCP tool for them (source checked 2026-10-05).

mimo-code.userNote: MiMo Code 0.1.15 cannot send a generic binary file to its model. It passes the file through unconverted and the model service can refuse the whole request, so LeapMux refuses the file first.
mimo-code.detailNote:
The current MiMo Code attachment path refuses arbitrary binary bytes. It does not convert a filename into usable binary input.

Classified as an agent limit: MiMo Code keeps the OpenCode mapping of media types to input kinds (provider/transform.ts mimeToModality, source revision 698f0f2), so a generic binary file has no input kind and reaches the model adapter unconverted (checked 2026-10-05).

Tested version: MiMo Code 0.1.15.

qwen-code.userNote: Qwen Code 0.24.7 turns a binary file that is not an image, audio, video, or PDF into a text placeholder before the model sees it. LeapMux refuses the upload.
qwen-code.detailNote:
Qwen replaces unsupported binary media with a document placeholder in its model request. The model does not receive the file bytes.

Classified as an agent limit: Qwen Code 0.24.7 (openaiContentGenerator/converter.ts) returns the text 'Unsupported inline media type' or 'Unsupported file media type' for any MIME type other than image, audio, video, or PDF. The model never receives the bytes. LeapMux refuses generic binary input in qwenProvider.ValidateAttachment (checked 2026-10-05).

oh-my-pi.userNote: Oh My Pi accepts text and images as input. It has no input type for binary files other than images, so LeapMux refuses them. See the [Oh My Pi RPC documentation](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/rpc.md).
oh-my-pi.detailNote:
The current Oh My Pi attachment path refuses arbitrary binary bytes. It does not convert a filename into usable binary input.

Classified as an agent limit: the prompt, steer and follow_up commands of Oh My Pi 18.6.0 take a message and an images field (ImageContent[]), and its wire user content type is text or image. It has no field for other binary data (documentation checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/rpc.md>: The prompt command schema takes message and images (ImageContent[]). The wire content type is text or image only.

kiro.userNote: Kiro reads Word and Excel files, but drops other binary files, such as an archive. LeapMux refuses every binary file and does not send Word or Excel files yet.
kiro.detailNote:
The current Kiro attachment path refuses arbitrary binary bytes. It does not convert a filename into usable binary input.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with medium confidence: KAS 0.66.8 (Kiro CLI 2.24.0) accepts a resource blob only for application/pdf, text/csv, text/html, text/plain, text/markdown, msword, docx, vnd.ms-excel, and xlsx, and drops every other blob without a message. LeapMux classifies Word and Excel files as binary and refuses them in kiroProvider.ValidateAttachment. The spec uses a generic .bin file, which Kiro drops, so the unsupported verdict holds (checked 2026-10-05).

amp.userNote: Amp's stream input accepts only text and images, so LeapMux cannot send any other binary file to Amp. LeapMux refuses the attachment. See [Amp's streaming JSON documentation](https://ampcode.com/docs/cli/streaming-json).
amp.detailNote:
The current Amp attachment path refuses arbitrary binary bytes. It does not convert a filename into usable binary input.

Classified as an agent limit: the stdin schema of Amp 0.0.1791074829 stream-JSON takes text blocks and base64 image blocks only (checked 2026-10-05 in the documentation and in the installed CLI bundle). A malformed line ends the Amp session, so LeapMux refuses the file before it writes the line.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://ampcode.com/docs/cli/streaming-json>: The stream JSON input schema lists text blocks and image blocks only.

cline.userNote: Cline accepts only text files and images as input, and it refuses a file that holds binary data. LeapMux refuses any other binary attachment.
cline.detailNote:
The current Cline attachment path refuses arbitrary binary bytes. It does not convert a filename into usable binary input.

Classified as an agent limit: Cline 3.0.68 reads an attached file as text and refuses a file with a NUL byte; its own `read_files` tool states that it does not support binary files other than images (source checked 2026-10-05).

junie.userNote: Junie documents image input only, so LeapMux refuses a binary file that is not an image.
junie.detailNote:
Junie exposes no supported other binary input through this integration. LeapMux refuses the upload and keeps the actual file bytes out of the next native model request.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: Junie 26.9.22 documents image inputs only. It stores an inline blob as a temporary file for its text tools. LeapMux refuses the upload before the request, so the agent was not tried with a binary file (checked 2026-10-05).

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code accepts only text and images in a message. It has no input for other binary files, so LeapMux refuses such an upload.
letta-code.detailNote:
Letta Code exposes no supported other binary input through this integration. LeapMux refuses the upload and keeps the actual file bytes out of the next native model request.

Classified as an agent limit: Letta Code 0.34.2 accepts text parts and base64 image parts in a message (installed letta.js checked 2026-10-05).

dirac.userNote: Dirac reads only the text and images of a message. It drops the bytes of any other binary file, so LeapMux refuses to attach one.
dirac.detailNote:
Dirac exposes no supported other binary input through this integration. LeapMux refuses the upload and keeps the actual file bytes out of the next native model request.

Classified as an agent limit. Dirac 0.5.17 parsePromptContent keeps text blocks, image blocks and only the URI of an embedded resource. Its ACP prompt capabilities state audio false (upstream source checked 2026-10-05). No route carries other binary bytes to the model.

qoder-cli.userNote: Qoder CLI reads only text and image blocks in its stream JSON input. It cannot represent another binary file as model input, so LeapMux refuses such an upload.
qoder-cli.detailNote:
Qoder's prompt parser ignores inline PDF and binary blocks. Its file-upload path requires a separate file identifier that LeapMux does not create.

Classified as an agent limit: the stream JSON input of Qoder CLI 1.1.65 carries text and image blocks only (installed binary strings checked 2026-10-05).

factory-droid.userNote: Factory Droid accepts only images, PDF files, and plain text as attached input. It has no input for any other binary file, so LeapMux refuses such an upload.
factory-droid.detailNote:
Factory Droid exposes no supported other binary input through this integration. LeapMux refuses the upload and keeps the actual file bytes out of the next native model request.

Classified as an agent limit: Droid 0.233.0 message input accepts image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp, application/pdf, and text/plain only (installed binary strings checked 2026-10-05).

fast-agent.userNote: Fast Agent turns most binary files into a placeholder text, so the model does not see their bytes. LeapMux refuses to attach them.
fast-agent.detailNote:
Fast Agent exposes no supported other binary input through this integration. LeapMux refuses the upload and keeps the actual file bytes out of the next native model request.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. Fast Agent 0.10.42 declares audio false in its ACP prompt capabilities. Its OpenAI-style converter writes [Binary resource: name (type)] for an embedded blob, unless the type is an image, a PDF, a video type or text (source checked 2026-10-05). Some model routes accept audio or video bytes. The tested OpenAI-style route does not accept a generic binary file.

deepseek-harness.userNote: DeepSeek Harness saves an attached binary file and gives the model a handle. The model reads the bytes with a tool, so the content reaches the model one request later.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-file-attachments-probe: native upload saved exact file bytes. The model received its native handle. A real read or Bash byte read returned the complete content in the second model request. Each case made two requests with no unexpected request. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI accepts audio input, such as a WAV file. LeapMux does not verify other binary file types.
gemini-cli.detailNote: The positive case uses a valid PCM WAV. Installed ACP advertises audio input. The browser spec requires audio/wav and exact decoded native bytes. This does not claim opaque .bin acceptance.

command-code.userNote: Command Code's JSON-RPC mode accepts only text and images, so LeapMux cannot send it another binary file. LeapMux refuses the attachment.
command-code.detailNote:
The native RPC parseBlock accepts text and base64 images only. It rejects generic binary blocks.

Classified as an agent limit: parseBlock in Command Code 1.74.1 (dist/cli.mjs, checked 2026-10-05) throws invalid params for any block that is not a text block or a base64 image block. LeapMux rejects the attachment before it sends the turn.

muse-code.userNote: Muse MSP input accepts text and images only; its media/upload route carries video alone. LeapMux refuses binary attachments.
muse-code.detailNote: Muse MSP input accepts text and images only; its media/upload route carries video alone. LeapMux refuses binary attachments. The deciding evidence came from the binary itself: its exported MSP schema and a live muse serve probe under the local mock.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix sends the picture from its image tool to the model, but its tool update to LeapMux holds text only. LeapMux cannot show the image.
reasonix.detailNote:
Reasonix sends a `view_image` picture to its model, but its ACP tool update contains text only. LeapMux cannot show the image in that tool row.

Classified as an agent limit: the Reasonix 1.38.7 dispatch code builds text content for a tool result and has no image block, although view_image returns image bytes to the model (source read 2026-10-05).

zcode.userNote: ZCode returns a tool result as text only. LeapMux still shows the picture, because ZCode saves it with the tool call.
zcode.detailNote:
A tool result arrives as text, and LeapMux restores the picture from ZCode's stored attachment records.

This cell covers pictures in tool results: ZCode returns a tool result as text, and LeapMux restores the picture from the saved tool record. Prompt image attachments are a separate feature (image-attachments).

codewhale.userNote: CodeWhale reports the image that a tool returns. LeapMux checks the image and shows it in the tool row.
codewhale.detailNote: Codewhale publishes immutable tool image records. LeapMux stores verified image bytes beside the native tool event. See providers/codewhale/media.go.

qwen-code.userNote: Qwen Code gives its model the image that a tool reads, but it sends LeapMux only a text description of it. LeapMux cannot show the image in the tool row.
qwen-code.detailNote:
Qwen Code converts a Read image for its model, but its ACP tool update carries text without image bytes. LeapMux cannot show the image in that tool row.

Classified as an agent limit: the ACP tool-call emitter and the text projection of Qwen Code 0.24.7 contain no image or inlineData handling. The spec shows that the model request carries the JPEG. The tool row holds only the 'Image overview: 64x64' text (checked 2026-10-05).

amp.userNote: LeapMux draws an image that Amp's `Read` tool returns. Amp's current modes offer no `Read` tool, so this applies to threads that still use it. An Amp MCP tool result is text only, so no image appears there.
amp.detailNote:
An Amp MCP result is text only; a `Read` of an image file does render.

The verdict is supported, with low confidence. The spec scripts a `Read` call through the mock service. The init tool list and `amp tools list` of a real Amp (research and probes, version 0.0.1790208065) show no `Read` tool. Amp's image tool is the server-side `view_media`, and no spec checks how its result reaches the stream (checked 2026-10-05). Open question for the maintainers: whether this cell stays supported.

cline.userNote: When the model accepts images, Cline's file tool returns the bytes of an image file. LeapMux does not draw that image yet, so the tool row shows text only.
cline.detailNote:
It draws no image from a tool result.

The worker persists the whole `tool.finished` event as Cline sent it (`closeToolRow` stores the raw envelope), so image data is stored; only the reader draws no image. Classified as a LeapMux limit: `read_files` of Cline 3.0.68 returns `[{query, result: ['Successfully read image', {type: 'image', data, mediaType}], success}]` when the model supports images, and the hub forwards the output in `tool.finished`. The LeapMux reader always returns an empty image list. Medium confidence: the E2E spec never produced the image shape (source checked 2026-10-05).

codebuddy-code.userNote: CodeBuddy Code sends the image from its Read tool to the model separately. Its stream gives LeapMux only a text placeholder for the tool result, so the tool row shows no image.
codebuddy-code.detailNote:
CodeBuddy Code sends Read image bytes to its model through a separate input. Its stream gives LeapMux only a text placeholder for that tool result, so the tool row cannot show the image.

Classified as an agent limit: the E2E model request of CodeBuddy 2.160.0 holds the image data URL in a trailing user row. The stream result carries no image bytes, and the tool row shows only the file name and a text result. The agent keeps image bytes in its own blob store and sends the model a separate input.

junie.userNote: Junie gives its model the image that an MCP tool returns, but it sends LeapMux an empty tool result. LeapMux cannot show the image in the tool row.
junie.detailNote:
Junie sends an MCP tool's PNG bytes to its model, but its ACP tool call and update carry `content:[]`. LeapMux receives no image bytes to show in the tool row.

Classified as an agent limit: the spec shows the PNG bytes in the next model request, while the Junie 26.9.22 tool call and update carry an empty content array, so no image bytes reach LeapMux (checked 2026-10-05).

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code sends the picture from a `ViewImage` call to its model. Its live output to LeapMux holds only the text of the result, so LeapMux shows no image in the result row.
letta-code.detailNote:
Letta Code sends a `ViewImage` picture to its model.

Classified as an agent limit with low confidence: the live tool return of Letta Code 0.34.2 keeps only text parts (installed letta.js checked 2026-10-05). The stored message projection of its local store (toolResultToStoredReturnValue) keeps image parts, and LeapMux never reads that store for tool results. The live tool return drops image parts, but the stored projection of the Letta local store keeps them. A LeapMux limit is the alternative classification, because that stored projection keeps the image. Not run natively.

dirac.userNote: Dirac passes the image that a tool reads to its model, but it sends no image to LeapMux, so the tool row shows no image.
dirac.detailNote:
The native result reaches the next model request, but its tool transcript contains no inline image before or after reload.

Classified as an agent limit. The Dirac 0.5.17 ACP translator builds tool content from text and diff blocks only. It has no image block (upstream source checked 2026-10-05). The E2E run shows that the model receives the result and that the transcript has no image before or after a reload. The read tool sends an image extension to a local rich-file reader (extractFileContent, which reads the file with fs and builds an image block for the model). It does not use the ACP text file route, which carries text files only (source checked 2026-10-05).

deepseek-harness.userNote: LeapMux shows an image that the `read_image` tool returns, taken from the files that DeepSeek Harness saves.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-image-probe: actual read_image and session/attachment returned 168 bytes for a 64x64 image. The content hash matched the native ID. A foreign Session received ATTACHMENT_NOT_REFERENCED. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: When Gemini CLI reads an image file, LeapMux shows the image in the tool result. The image stays after a reload.
gemini-cli.detailNote: Native read_file stores the image bytes in its JSONL response. LeapMux recovers those exact bytes beside the unchanged ACP frame and retains them after reload.

command-code.userNote: LeapMux shows an image that an MCP tool returns. Command Code compresses an image that it reads, so LeapMux shows the compressed picture.
command-code.detailNote: The installed MCP image probe returns an image content block. Native tool_completed preserves that block and the next model request contains its image. The CLI compresses a read image before it attaches it, and the native result states the attached bytes.

muse-code.userNote: Muse's read of an image hands its bytes to the next model request as an image part; the tool result states the file and media type as text alone, so the row draws no picture.
muse-code.detailNote: Muse's read of an image hands its bytes to the next model request as an image part; the tool result states the file and media type as text alone, so the row draws no picture. The deciding evidence came from the binary itself: its exported MSP schema and a live muse serve probe under the local mock.

junie.userNote: Junie 26.9.22 does not send the reasoning that its model returns, so the transcript shows no thinking. The answer still appears.
junie.detailNote:
Junie's ACP bridge sends no thought update for a Responses reasoning item. The model answer still reaches LeapMux.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: a Responses model returned a reasoning item. Junie 26.9.22 sent no agent_thought_chunk for it, and the answer reached LeapMux. Only the OpenAI Responses wire was tried (checked 2026-10-05).

deepseek-harness.userNote: DeepSeek Harness sends reasoning as its own block in the assistant message, and LeapMux shows it in the transcript.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-turn-probe: separate native reasoning and text blocks in one assistant message. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: LeapMux shows the thoughts of the model as a separate row. The row stays after a reload.
gemini-cli.detailNote: Native Google thought parts become ACP thought chunks and original JSONL thoughts. The browser spec requires a separate thought row and persistence after reload.

command-code.userNote: LeapMux shows the thinking text that Command Code reports for a turn.
command-code.detailNote: The installed basic probe emits thinking_start, thinking_delta and thinking_end. LeapMux stores the native thinking rows and does not duplicate message_update snapshots.

cursor.userNote: Cursor 2026.09.28 sends no context usage over the connection that LeapMux uses, so Agent info shows no context count. Cursor shows it only in its own terminal interface. A [feature request](https://forum.cursor.com/t/cli-emit-acp-usage-update-so-clients-like-zed-can-show-a-context-window-indicator/165358) is open.
cursor.detailNote:
The installed Cursor CLI's ACP bridge sends no usage update after a model turn. LeapMux cannot show the context count on this path.

Classified as an agent limit: Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 never sends usage_update, and a Cursor staff reply in the forum thread states that agent acp does not send it (installed bundle read and thread fetched 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://forum.cursor.com/t/cli-emit-acp-usage-update-so-clients-like-zed-can-show-a-context-window-indicator/165358> (open): A feature request asks Cursor CLI to emit usage_update over ACP. A Cursor staff reply says agent acp does not send it and gives no timeline.

codewhale.userNote: The Context card shows CodeWhale's own estimate of the whole context and its window, not the token counts of a single request.
codewhale.detailNote: The card shows the runtime's own context estimate and window from GET /v1/threads/{id}/context, not the counts of one request.

qoder-cli.userNote: Qoder reports context use as a ratio. LeapMux shows the percentage in Agent info and shows no token totals when Qoder sends none.
qoder-cli.detailNote: Qoder reports context occupancy as a ratio. LeapMux shows its percentage in Agent info without inventing token totals when Qoder omits them.

deepseek-harness.userNote: Agent info shows the token counts that DeepSeek Harness reports. The usage data has no context window, so LeapMux takes the window from another message that DeepSeek Harness sends.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-quota-headers-probe emits request/context with contextWindow=1000000 and assistant/message.data.usage with inputTokens=1, outputTokens=1, totalTokens=2. These are actual durable native events. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84. The Worker adds the native request/context window to each assistant block supplement.

gemini-cli.userNote: Agent info shows the token counts that Gemini CLI reports for the last request. It does not add up earlier turns.
gemini-cli.detailNote: Native usageMetadata supplies last-request input/output/cache counts. LeapMux reads that request, rather than summing prior turns.

command-code.userNote: Agent info shows the input, output, and cache token counts that Command Code reports. The context limit comes from the model data of the agent.
command-code.detailNote: Native model_request_end reports input, output, cache-read and cache-write tokens. Native model metadata supplies the context limit. LeapMux preserves the native usage values.

muse-code.userNote: Muse counts its own occupancy from the provider-reported facts: a model reply that states zero usage still leaves the host accounting above zero, so no zero reading exists to preserve.
muse-code.detailNote: Muse counts its own occupancy from the provider-reported facts: a model reply that states zero usage still leaves the host accounting above zero, so no zero reading exists to preserve.

cursor.userNote: Cursor 2026.09.28 reports no finished compaction over the connection that LeapMux uses, so LeapMux shows no compaction notice.
cursor.detailNote:
On these LeapMux paths, native compaction produces no completed event that the chat renders as a notice. A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as an agent limit: the Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 ACP presenter forwards no compaction or summary event, and its sessionUpdate kinds include none for compaction (installed bundle read 2026-10-05).

kilo.userNote: Kilo reports a finished compaction on its event stream, but LeapMux does not read that event from Kilo yet. The chat therefore shows no compaction notice.
kilo.detailNote:
On these LeapMux paths, native compaction produces no completed event that the chat renders as a notice. A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: Kilo 7.8.1 publishes session.compacted after a successful compaction (session/compaction.ts at tag v7.8.1). The ACP adapter handles session.status, permission.asked, message.updated, message.part.updated, and message.part.delta only. LeapMux reads the daemon stream for questions only (checked 2026-10-05). The state depends on counting the daemon event stream as part of the native protocol.

opencode.userNote: OpenCode reports a finished compaction on its event stream, but LeapMux does not read that event from OpenCode yet. The chat therefore shows no compaction notice.
opencode.detailNote:
On these LeapMux paths, native compaction produces no completed event that the chat renders as a notice. A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: OpenCode 1.18.34 publishes the session.compacted event after a successful compaction (session/compaction.ts). The ACP adapter handles only session.status, permission.asked, message.part.updated, and message.part.delta. The LeapMux daemon reader handles question events only (checked 2026-10-05). The state depends on counting the daemon event stream as part of the native protocol.

goose.userNote: Goose reports a finished compaction, and LeapMux shows the notice. The next model request uses the new summary.
goose.detailNote: Goose reports Compaction complete after its native summary. The next native model request uses that summary.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix reports a finished compaction only as a plain text line in its reply, so LeapMux shows no compaction notice.
reasonix.detailNote:
On these LeapMux paths, native compaction produces no completed event that the chat renders as a notice. A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as an agent limit: Reasonix 1.38.7 dispatch.go turns event.CompactionDone into the agent_message_chunk '[compacted N earlier messages to save context]' and states in a comment that ACP has no compaction-card concept (source read 2026-10-05).

codewhale.userNote: CodeWhale 0.10.0 reports a completed compaction. LeapMux shows one notice that states whether the compaction was manual or automatic.
codewhale.detailNote: CodeWhale 0.10.0 sends item.completed for context_compaction with the text Compaction complete. LeapMux draws one completed notice labeled manual.

mimo-code.userNote: MiMo Code reports compaction when it starts and when it ends. LeapMux shows one notice, with the summary, when it ends.
mimo-code.detailNote: MiMo Code sends its compaction part at the start and at the end. The end part carries the summary. LeapMux draws one completed notice.

qwen-code.userNote: Qwen Code reports when a compaction finishes. LeapMux shows that as a plain status line, not as a compaction notice.
qwen-code.detailNote:
A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: Qwen Code 0.24.7 sends _meta.contextCompression with phase 'done' and the original and new token counts after /compress (research qwen-code.md section 5.4). LeapMux reads it in qwen/output.go reportCompression and persists the agent status line 'Context compacted from A to B tokens'; it draws no compaction divider. Qwen Code does send a completed event (phase done), and LeapMux shows it as a status line. Open question for the maintainers: the feature definition may count that status line as a notice, which would make this cell supported.

grok-build.userNote: Grok Build reports when a compaction finishes, with the token counts before and after. LeapMux shows that as a plain status line, not as a compaction notice.
grok-build.detailNote:
A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: Grok Build 1.0.46 emits _x.ai/session_notification auto_compact_completed {tokens_before, tokens_after} for /compact and for auto-compaction. LeapMux persists the agent status line 'Context compacted from A to B tokens' and draws no compaction divider. Grok Build does send auto_compact_completed, and LeapMux shows it as a status line. Open question for the maintainers: the feature definition may count that status line as a notice, which would make this cell supported.

kiro.userNote: Kiro reports when a compaction finishes. LeapMux shows that as the plain status line 'Context compacted', not as a compaction notice.
kiro.detailNote:
A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: KAS 0.66.8 sends session_info_update summarization_completed after /compact and after auto-compaction. LeapMux persists the agent status line 'Context compacted' and draws no compaction divider. The spec itself requires that line to be visible. Kiro does send summarization_completed, and LeapMux shows it as a status line. Open question for the maintainers: the feature definition may count that status line as a notice, which would make this cell supported.

amp.userNote: Amp compacts a long thread on its own server and prints no compaction event in its stream, so LeapMux shows no compaction notice.
amp.detailNote:
On these LeapMux paths, native compaction produces no completed event that the chat renders as a notice. A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as an agent limit: Amp 0.0.1791074829 stream-JSON prints init, user, assistant, and result lines only. The server events `compaction_started` and `compaction_complete` never reach stdout (installed bundle and research probes, checked 2026-10-05).

codebuddy-code.userNote: CodeBuddy Code runs `/compact` in stream-JSON mode but reports no finished compaction. It sends only a compacting status that clears afterwards, so LeapMux shows no compaction notice.
codebuddy-code.detailNote:
CodeBuddy Code runs `/compact` in stream-JSON mode, but that stream reports no compaction notice. LeapMux cannot show a notice for it.

Classified as an agent limit: the stream writer of CodeBuddy 2.160.0 emits system status 'compacting' and then status null, and no boundary frame (binary check, 2026-10-05). A start status alone does not satisfy the feature definition.

junie.userNote: Junie 26.9.22 sends no compaction event. Its `/compress` command only acknowledges the request, so the transcript shows no compaction notice.
junie.detailNote:
On these LeapMux paths, native compaction produces no completed event that the chat renders as a notice. A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: Junie 26.9.22 answers protocol version 1. Its update kinds have no compaction update. The compaction_update kind exists only in the version 2 types, which this build does not negotiate. /compress answers 'Context will be compressed before the next task' and makes no model request (checked 2026-10-05).

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code reports a finished compaction with a summary, but LeapMux does not show it as a notice yet.
letta-code.detailNote:
A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the Letta Code 0.34.2 local backend streams an event_message (compaction) and a summary_message when it compacts, and the Letta adapter has no reader for them (installed letta.js and LeapMux source checked 2026-10-05). Letta Code produces completed compaction events, and LeapMux does not render them. Not run natively.

dirac.userNote: After Dirac condenses the conversation, the chat shows a Conversation Condensed notice.
dirac.detailNote: The native condense operation shows Conversation Condensed in the chat after completion. The native smol case also proves the condensed next model context.

qoder-cli.userNote: Qoder reports a finished compaction, and LeapMux shows it as a notice. Qoder refuses `/compact` when its token count says the summary would not reduce the context, for example in a short session. A refusal shows no completed notice.
qoder-cli.detailNote: Qoder emits a `compact_boundary` after successful native compaction. It refuses `/compact` when its token count says the summary would not reduce context. A short session or a model that reports too few input tokens can cause this refusal. A refusal shows no completed notice.

fast-agent.userNote: Fast Agent compacts its history by itself when the context is nearly full. It sends LeapMux no completed event, so the chat shows no notice.
fast-agent.detailNote:
On these LeapMux paths, native compaction produces no completed event that the chat renders as a notice. A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. Fast Agent 0.10.42 turns auto-compaction on by default at 85 percent of the context window. Its hook prints the result through the console display, not through an ACP update (source checked 2026-10-05). The guide describes the result display for the terminal interface and the Harness API only. No run of an automatic compaction was done.

deepseek-harness.userNote: LeapMux shows a notice when DeepSeek Harness finishes a compaction.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-compaction-probe: six actual native preparation turns, native summarizer, one completed compaction boundary, and the next request. Eight strict mock requests. The next request contained the new summary and omitted the old marker. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84. The /compact command runs inside commands/execute, with compaction events and no turn events.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI compacts its context on its own, but it does not report this to LeapMux, so the chat shows no notice.
gemini-cli.detailNote:
The ACP prompt event switch omits ChatCompressed. Native automatic compaction does not produce a completed ACP notice.

Classified as an agent limit. The ACP prompt loop of Gemini CLI 0.62.0 handles nine event types: content, thought, tool call request, finished, model info, max session turns, loop detected, context window overflow and error. It does not handle the chat-compressed event, which only its terminal interface handles (upstream source checked 2026-10-05).

command-code.userNote: LeapMux shows a compaction notice after a manual `/compact` that Command Code summarized, and after an automatic trim that saved tokens. A failed attempt shows no notice.
command-code.detailNote: The native manual summarized outcome supplies the completed notice. Native compaction_done also runs after failure, so the reader does not treat a manual finish event as success. Positive automatic trim savings remain a completed boundary.

muse-code.userNote: The private settings declare a config model catalog with context limits, so the host compaction thresholds resolve and /compact runs the native summarizer (generate_summary).
muse-code.detailNote: The private settings declare a config model catalog with context limits, so the host compaction thresholds resolve and /compact runs the native summarizer (generate_summary). The deciding evidence came from the binary itself: its exported MSP schema and a live muse serve probe under the local mock.

codex.userNote: After compaction, Codex keeps your earlier prompts in the next request. It replaces its earlier answers with a summary.
codex.detailNote: Codex keeps the original user prompts in the next model request after native compaction. It replaces the earlier assistant turns with a handoff summary.

cursor.userNote: Cursor 2026.09.28 has no compaction command over the connection that LeapMux uses. LeapMux sends `/compact` to the model as plain text, and Cursor does not compact.
cursor.detailNote:
Cursor sends `/compact` to the model as ordinary text on LeapMux's ACP path. It emits no native compaction result.

Classified as an agent limit: the Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 ACP agent resolves only /copy-request-id and user-defined commands, so /compact reaches the model as text (installed bundle read 2026-10-05).

github-copilot.userNote: After compaction, Copilot removes the older turns. Its summary can quote your earlier prompts, so their text can remain.
github-copilot.detailNote: Copilot removes the old standalone turns. Its native summary can quote the original user prompt, so the prompt text can remain inside the summary.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix 1.38.7 runs `/compact` only in its own interfaces. Over the connection that LeapMux uses, Reasonix sends `/compact` to the model as plain text.
reasonix.detailNote:
Reasonix sends `/compact` to the model as ordinary text on LeapMux's ACP path. Its desktop command is unavailable on that path.

Classified as an agent limit: Reasonix 1.38.7 sessionPrompt calls ctrl.RunTurn with the text, and resolveSlashPrompt resolves only custom commands, skills, MCP prompts, and extension actions, while Controller.Submit (not used by ACP) is the code that routes /compact (source read 2026-10-05).

amp.userNote: Amp has no command that LeapMux can use to compact a thread. `/compact` reaches Amp as ordinary text, and Amp compacts a thread only by itself on its server.
amp.detailNote:
Amp sends `/compact` to the model as ordinary text in stream mode. It emits no native compaction result.

Classified as an agent limit: the CLI command list and the client message list of Amp 0.0.1791074829 hold no compaction trigger, and `threads handoff` and `threads fork` are removed or deprecated (installed bundle, checked 2026-10-05). The E2E spec shows the `/compact` text reaching the model request unchanged.

cline.userNote: Cline compacts a long conversation on its own. Its `/compact` command works only in Cline's own terminal interface, so LeapMux sends `/compact` to the model as ordinary text. See [Cline's terminal UI documentation](https://docs.cline.bot/usage/tui).
cline.detailNote:
Cline's hub treats `/compact` as a model prompt. The CLI's local command is unavailable through the hub connection that LeapMux drives.

Classified as an agent limit: Cline 3.0.68 hub commands hold `session.compaction.get` and `session.compaction.update` (store a compaction state) but no command that asks the daemon to compact; the CLI builds the summary in its own process and stores the state. A LeapMux route would have to summarize the conversation itself, which is an emulation that LeapMux does not build (source checked 2026-10-05). Medium confidence because of that route.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://docs.cline.bot/usage/tui>: The Cline terminal UI lists /compact among its slash commands.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: the spec sends /compress to Junie 26.9.22 and sees no model request. Two later requests still hold the old marker and the prior solution. Compression through ACP may need a later build or a larger history (checked 2026-10-05).

The compact command returns a result. A plain text input that starts with /compact reaches the model as ordinary text only because LeapMux sends it that way. Not run natively.

Fast Agent's ACP path returns `Unknown command: /compact` for the manual command.

cursor.detailNote:
Cursor's ACP bridge returns a native quota failure but sends no quota window to LeapMux. The Agent info card shows no rate-limit state.

opencode.detailNote:

goose.detailNote:
Goose receives quota headers from the model service but reports no quota window through this LeapMux integration. The Agent info card shows no rate-limit state.

Classified as an agent limit: the Goose 1.53.0 ACP server and its custom request types have no rate-limit or quota field (source searched 2026-10-05). The E2E spec sends quota headers from the mock model service, and Goose publishes no quota window.

pi.userNote: Pi reports no quota or rate-limit window to its client, so Agent info shows none. Upstream closed [a request for a rate-limit event](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9704) as not planned.
pi.detailNote:
Pi receives quota headers from the model service but reports no quota window through this LeapMux integration. The Agent info card shows no rate-limit state.

Classified as an agent limit: no command or event in the Pi 1.0.0 RPC documentation returns a quota window, a rate-limit state or a reset time. get_session_stats returns token counts, cost and context usage only (documentation checked 2026-10-05). Extension code can read the response headers of a provider through the after_provider_response hook, and upstream issue 9704 asks for a provider-neutral rate-limit event and is closed as not planned. A LeapMux extension that forwards the headers would be an emulation that LeapMux does not build.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9704> (closed): Asks for a provider-neutral rate-limit telemetry hook for extensions, because after_provider_response gives HTTP and SSE headers only. Closed as not planned.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix reports no quota window or reset time to LeapMux, so Agent info shows no rate limit.
reasonix.detailNote:
Reasonix receives quota headers from the model service but reports no quota window through this LeapMux integration. The Agent info card shows no rate-limit state.

Classified as an agent limit: the Reasonix 1.38.7 ACP session status and usage objects hold token counts and cost, with no quota window (source searched 2026-10-05). The source has no code that reads quota headers (it handles only HTTP 429 text). Receiving quota headers from the model service therefore does not mean that Reasonix uses them.

zcode.userNote: ZCode 3.14.4 reports no quota window, usage, or reset time, so Agent info shows no rate-limit state. [An open upstream request](https://github.com/zai-org/feedback/issues/761) asks ZCode to show rate-limit usage.

Upstream issue zai-org/feedback#761 (open) reports that ZCode shows no rate-limit usage and that 429 replies carry no rate-limit headers. kimi-code.userNote: Kimi Code's server reports the quota windows of a signed-in Kimi Code account, with use and reset time, but LeapMux does not show them yet. See the [server API documentation](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/reference/server-api.html).
kimi-code.detailNote:
Native service failures can still appear in the transcript.

The Kimi server supplies the quota windows and the reset time through `GET /api/v1/oauth/usage`, and LeapMux never reads that route. Classified as a LeapMux limit: the server API of Kimi Code 2.1.1 documents `GET /api/v1/oauth/usage`, which returns `{ usedRatio, resetAt }` for each quota window of the account (`limit5h`, `limit7d`, `monthTotal`, `monthCode`); LeapMux never calls it (documentation, source, and installed build checked 2026-10-05). The route covers managed accounts that signed in with OAuth, so a user with an API key gets no data; the E2E fixture uses a mock model and cannot reach it. Medium confidence for that reason.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/reference/server-api.html>: GET /api/v1/oauth/usage returns the plan quota: one usedRatio and resetAt entry for each quota window (limit5h, limit7d, monthTotal, monthCode) and an optional wallet.

gemini-cli.detailNote: Native closed-session proof uses installed 0.62.0 and the strict local mock. A session closed and reopened inside the same UTC minute fails native session/load with -32603 (No previous sessions found), because 0.62.0 names its archive for the minute and appends to the original file; upstream fixed that collision in [upstream fix](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/29463) ([native session issue](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/28693)), first released in v0.63.0-preview.0; stable 0.62.0 does NOT carry the fix, so the browser spec reopens a session archived in an earlier minute. A session from an earlier minute loads, and the reopened tab restores the stored LeapMux transcript and serves the next model request with the original native context. Gemini also starts native history replay without awaiting completion ([history replay issue](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/28775)), so replayed text can trail the session/load reply; the worker consumes that idle replay for the current session instead of storing it beside the copied transcript, and a prompt never inherits text buffered before it started.

The Bypass permissions shortcut is the plus-menu / banner control that switches the session to the provider's own bypass mode. A provider whose plugin declares no permission preset renders no shortcut, whatever its CLI can do.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: Qoder CLI 1.1.65 has the bypass_permissions mode (yolo) in its launch flags, its permission mode parser, and its session metadata, and the SDK documents bypassPermissions over the same stream protocol (installed binary strings and docs.qoder.com checked 2026-10-05). A mode change in a running session through set_permission_mode was not verified. LeapMux offers five modes (default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, plan) and no bypass. The Qoder plugin declares a Smart preset and no Bypass preset. Not run natively.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://docs.qoder.com/cli/permissions>: Lists six permission modes, including bypass_permissions (YOLO), and the flags --permission-mode bypass_permissions, --yolo, and --dangerously-skip-permissions.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with medium confidence. Fast Agent 0.10.42 documents --no-permissions as a launch flag of its ACP command. The docs say: Disable prompts entirely, all tools are allowed (upstream docs checked 2026-10-05). The LeapMux launch passes no such flag. The Fast Agent plugin declares no permission preset. The flag needs a restart of the process.

command-code.userNote: The model list holds the models that the Command Code service offers to your account and the models that you declare with your own keys. A model switch can restart the session. It keeps the effort when the new model offers it, and it resets the effort to Auto otherwise.
command-code.detailNote: The native session/set_model RPC applies model changes. The native bundle lists 86 selectable gateway models. The live catalog omits them in local-only mode and includes native BYOK declarations. Gateway choices require Command Code service access. The native set_model call refuses a BYOK model that the live gateway list omits, so LeapMux restarts the session. A model switch keeps the effort when the live catalog lists the new model and offers the tier. When the catalog omits the model (local-only mode) or lacks the tier, the switch resets the effort to Auto, and the relaunch passes no --effort. After startup, LeapMux confirms the launch effort through session/set_effort, because the host can report another effort in its first state.

kilo.userNote: Needs a Kilo that lists the `/goal` command, as Kilo 7.8.1 does. Pause and resume use the same command. LeapMux draws the goal controls only while Kilo lists it.
kilo.detailNote:
Claude Code, Goose, Kilo, Qwen Code and Grok Build take a goal only when their CLI advertises its `goal` command. Kimi Code takes one only while the engine's goal feature runs. Kilo 7.8.1 defines the built-in goal command with the hint '<objective | pause | resume | clear>' (command/index.ts at tag v7.8.1).

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix 1.38.7 has no pause or resume for a goal over the connection that LeapMux uses ([issue](https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/issues/10201)). Reasonix 2.x adds both, and LeapMux does not use them yet.
