Classified as an agent limit for Reasonix 1.38.7: its ACP offers set_mode only. Issue #10201 (filed for the LeapMux maintainers) closed with pull request #10943, merged 2026-09-26 on the studio branch, which adds _reasonix.io/session/goal/pause and _reasonix.io/session/goal/resume; docs/ACP.md at v2.28.0 lists them and v1.39.7 does not. A retest with 2.x would make this a LeapMux limit (checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/issues/10201> (closed): The issue asks Reasonix to expose an explicit Goal resume operation, and a matching pause operation, over ACP. It closed with pull request #10943.

The parent consumes the native stopped report. Six strict mock requests, two exact parent reports, zero unexpected requests. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

command-code.detailNote: Native child start, background launch ID and stop events supply child task rows. The adapter retains early completion until the native launch ID arrives.

muse-code.userNote: A yielded bash command reports background_running through its result with no registry item; the workflow row is the background process the sidebar draws.
muse-code.detailNote: A yielded bash command reports background_running through its result with no registry item; the workflow row is the background process the sidebar draws.

amp.userNote: Amp's stream shows a subagent only as a call and a final report. It sends no messages and no session for the subagent, so LeapMux has no subagent tab for Amp.
amp.detailNote:
The stream also carries no child messages and no workflow activity.

Classified as an agent limit: the stream-JSON adapter of Amp 0.0.1791074829 ignores each message that has a `parentToolUseId`, so only the parent `tool_use` and the final `tool_result` of `Task`, `oracle`, `librarian`, and `finder` reach stdout (installed bundle, checked 2026-10-05). The internal thread-actor protocol does carry child messages, but it is undocumented and LeapMux does not speak it; medium confidence because of that alternative.

dirac.userNote: Each Dirac subagent opens its own tab. The tab shows the prompt and loads the full history when the subagent ends. Dirac does not stream the full transcript while the subagent runs.
dirac.detailNote: Dirac and Fast Agent open a child tab for each subagent. The tab shows its prompt and loads the native message history when the child ends. Neither agent streams its full child transcript while it runs. Fast Agent's [Agent Client Protocol (ACP) tracker](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/acp/tool_progress.py#L236-L260) creates a tool ID that differs from the model ID in its [child snapshot](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/agents/subagent_tool.py#L829-L833). Its [ACP completion](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/acp/tool_progress.py#L873-L900) sends result text without a child ID. When equal results cannot identify one archive, LeapMux closes the ambiguous child with an archive-unavailable report.

Its [ACP completion](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/acp/tool_progress.py#L873-L900) sends result text without a child ID. When equal results cannot identify one archive, LeapMux closes the ambiguous child with an archive-unavailable report.

deepseek-harness.userNote: The child tab shows the messages of the child agent and each later message that the parent agent sends to it. It hides the instruction and context messages that DeepSeek Harness injects.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-child-controls-probe: a real continuable child has its own live follow stream. Its completed first turn starts an exact parent report. Native subagents/prompt sends the next prompt to the same child; that request retains the old child answer. interruptByParent closes the second turn as aborted with cause user. The parent consumes the native stopped report. Six strict mock requests, two exact parent reports, zero unexpected requests. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84. The child tab shows the native prompt (source user, no rpcId). A later message of the parent agent from send_message is a user message with source agent-message in @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 (createAgentMessage, submitAdmitted). LeapMux stores it nowhere else for the child tab, so the tab keeps it. A Go unit test covers this input kind; no browser spec sends it. Injected instruction-file and runtime-context messages are not shown. A child message to the root session and the team-message kind of the experimental team profile are not stored; no probe has checked them.

gemini-cli.userNote: Each Gemini CLI subagent opens its own tab. Gemini CLI links a subagent to its root session and not to its direct parent.
gemini-cli.detailNote: Child UUID and owning root session are exact native storage identities. Gemini stores nested descendants under the root and omits direct-parent links.

command-code.userNote: The child tab holds the prompt that Command Code gave the child and its final report. Command Code sends no full child transcript.
command-code.detailNote: The native agent opener supplies the exact child prompt. The native tool result supplies the final report. LeapMux stores these in the child tab. The supported native API supplies no complete child text or tool-result transcript.

muse-code.userNote: Children run only inside workflow scripts; the fold carries a durable childId and lifecycle with no child session, so no transcript tab can exist.
muse-code.detailNote: Children run only inside workflow scripts; the fold carries a durable childId and lifecycle with no child session, so no transcript tab can exist. The deciding evidence came from the binary itself: its exported MSP schema and a live muse serve probe under the local mock.

cursor.userNote: Cursor streams the messages of a subagent while it runs, and LeapMux shows them in the subagent tab.
cursor.detailNote: The native Cursor subagent capability streams child messages before completion. LeapMux routes those messages to the child transcript. See providers/cursor/subagent.go.

kilo.userNote: Kilo runs a subagent as its own session and streams that session's messages on its event stream. LeapMux does not read those messages yet. The subagent tab shows only the prompt and the final report, and a background subagent shows only the prompt.
kilo.detailNote:
Kilo, OpenCode, Pi and Reasonix deliver the subagent's transcript when it completes: the prompt at spawn and the report at the end. A background spawn of Kilo, OpenCode or Reasonix keeps the prompt only.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: Kilo 7.8.1 runs each subagent as a child session and publishes its message events on the daemon event stream. The ACP adapter drops events of a session that it does not track, and LeapMux reads that stream for questions only (checked 2026-10-05). The state depends on counting the daemon event stream as part of the native protocol.

opencode.userNote: OpenCode runs a subagent as its own session and streams that session's messages on its event stream. LeapMux does not read those messages yet. The subagent tab shows only the prompt and the final report, and a background subagent shows only the prompt.
opencode.detailNote:
Kilo, OpenCode, Pi and Reasonix deliver the subagent's transcript when it completes: the prompt at spawn and the report at the end. A background spawn of Kilo, OpenCode or Reasonix keeps the prompt only.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: OpenCode 1.18.34 runs each subagent as a child session and publishes its message.part.updated events on the daemon event stream. The ACP adapter drops events of a session that it does not track, and LeapMux reads that stream for questions only (checked 2026-10-05). The state depends on counting the daemon event stream as part of the native protocol.

goose.userNote: LeapMux shows the tool calls of a Goose subagent while it runs. Goose sends no text from the subagent.
goose.detailNote: A transcript streams at message boundaries: a long text run appears when its message or turn ends. Goose streams the child's tool rows only, and its text never arrives. ZCode streams the tool cards live and sends the child's text as the final report. Codewhale and Qwen Code tail a transcript file, with about half a second of lag.

pi.userNote: The `pi-subagents` extension sends LeapMux progress counts and a final report for a subagent. The messages of a running subagent stay inside Pi. The child tab shows the prompt when the subagent starts and the report when it ends.
pi.detailNote:
Kilo, OpenCode, Pi and Reasonix deliver the subagent's transcript when it completes: the prompt at spawn and the report at the end. A background spawn of Kilo, OpenCode or Reasonix keeps the prompt only.

Classified as an agent limit: the foreground update of the Agent tool in pi-subagents carries tool use count, token count, status and an activity line, and no messages. The extension writes the transcript of each subagent to its own output file, and LeapMux reads no output file. The conversation viewer is a terminal-only overlay.

Tested version: Pi 1.0.0.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix gives LeapMux a subagent's report only when the subagent ends. LeapMux shows the prompt at the start and the report at the end. A background subagent shows its prompt only.
reasonix.detailNote:
Kilo, OpenCode, Pi and Reasonix deliver the subagent's transcript when it completes: the prompt at spawn and the report at the end. A background spawn of Kilo, OpenCode or Reasonix keeps the prompt only.

Classified as an agent limit: Reasonix 1.38.7 has no subagent update in its ACP code, so the child transcript exists only in the tool call and its final result (source searched 2026-10-05). LeapMux could read the child files from the Reasonix session store while the child runs, which would be an emulation that LeapMux does not build.

zcode.userNote: LeapMux shows the tool calls of a ZCode subagent while it runs. The subagent's text arrives as the final report.
zcode.detailNote: A transcript streams at message boundaries: a long text run appears when its message or turn ends. Goose streams the child's tool rows only, and its text never arrives. ZCode streams the tool cards live and sends the child's text as the final report. Codewhale and Qwen Code tail a transcript file, with about half a second of lag.

codewhale.userNote: LeapMux shows each message of a CodeWhale subagent when that message ends, with about half a second of lag.
codewhale.detailNote: A transcript streams at message boundaries: a long text run appears when its message or turn ends. Goose streams the child's tool rows only, and its text never arrives. ZCode streams the tool cards live and sends the child's text as the final report. Codewhale and Qwen Code tail a transcript file, with about half a second of lag.

qwen-code.userNote: LeapMux shows a long text run of a subagent when its message ends, not word by word. Rows of a background subagent lag by about half a second.
qwen-code.detailNote:
A transcript streams at message boundaries: a long text run appears when its message or turn ends. Goose streams the child's tool rows only, and its text never arrives. ZCode streams the tool cards live and sends the child's text as the final report. Codewhale and Qwen Code tail a transcript file, with about half a second of lag.

Qwen Code streams a foreground subagent in the parent session as session updates. LeapMux tails a transcript file only for a background subagent. The statement above that Qwen Code tails a transcript file therefore holds for background subagents only (checked 2026-10-05).

amp.userNote: Amp's stream drops the messages of a running subagent. LeapMux shows nothing from the subagent until its final report arrives in the result of the call.
amp.detailNote:
The stream also carries no child messages and no workflow activity.

Classified as an agent limit: Amp 0.0.1791074829 stream-JSON prints no child message while a subagent runs (installed bundle, checked 2026-10-05). The E2E spec shows the child model request while the parent transcript holds none of the child progress. The thread-actor protocol streams child deltas, but LeapMux does not speak it; medium confidence because of that alternative.

cline.userNote: LeapMux shows one running Cline subagent live. When two subagents run at the same time, their transcripts appear only when they finish.
cline.detailNote: Cline streams one subagent live. When two run at the same time, their transcripts appear when they finish.

dirac.userNote: While a Dirac subagent runs, its tab shows the prompt and short progress lines. Dirac gives the full tool transcript only after the subagent ends.
dirac.detailNote:
Dirac exposes the child prompt while the child runs, then restores its full tool transcript at the completed native archive boundary. A held native child Read produces no live tool row before that boundary.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. The Dirac 0.5.17 subagent card sends a trajectory of at most 80 events. Each text is cut to a fixed length. The card has no structured child tool rows (source checked 2026-10-05). LeapMux already shows the message and tool digest lines live. LeapMux restores the full tool transcript from the archive after the child ends. LeapMux drops the tool_result digest events, so a LeapMux limit is the alternative classification.

fast-agent.userNote: While a Fast Agent subagent runs, its tab shows the prompt. Fast Agent gives the full tool transcript only after the subagent ends.
fast-agent.detailNote:
Fast Agent exposes the child prompt while the child runs, then restores its full tool transcript at the completed native archive boundary. A held native child Read produces no live tool row before that boundary.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. Fast Agent 0.10.42 runs the child with one generate call and no tool execution handler. It writes the child session to disk (source checked 2026-10-05). The E2E run shows no live tool row before LeapMux reads the archive.

deepseek-harness.userNote: The child tab updates while the child works, including its tool activity, before its final report arrives.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-child-controls-probe: a real continuable child has its own live follow stream. Its completed first turn starts an exact parent report. Native subagents/prompt sends the next prompt to the same child; that request retains the old child answer. interruptByParent closes the second turn as aborted with cause user. The parent consumes the native stopped report. Six strict mock requests, two exact parent reports, zero unexpected requests. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: The tab of a Gemini CLI subagent fills while the subagent runs. Gemini CLI sends no live stream for a subagent, so LeapMux shows each completed model or tool step after Gemini CLI saves it.
gemini-cli.detailNote: Native JSONL records reach the child tab before final report completion. Native files supply completed model/tool records; ACP provides no child stream.

command-code.userNote: While a child runs, its tab shows short activity notices from Command Code. It shows no child text and no full tool result.
command-code.detailNote: The native subagent_progress event supplies abbreviated tool activity and token estimates. It drops child text and full tool results. The child tab shows each activity notice while the child runs, before its final report. It shows no child text and no full tool result.

muse-code.userNote: A workflow fold child owns no session, so no separate transcript receives its rows.
muse-code.detailNote: A workflow fold child owns no session, so no separate transcript receives its rows. The deciding evidence came from the binary itself: its exported MSP schema and a live muse serve probe under the local mock.

claude-code.userNote: Claude Code lets a user message a subagent in its own terminal app. The input stream that LeapMux uses cannot address one subagent, so the child tab is read-only.
claude-code.detailNote:
Claude Code's TUI can send a message to a Task subagent. It queues the message while the child runs or resumes an idle child. LeapMux drives Claude over stream-json stdin. Its user message carries no child or task ID, so typed input reaches the root session. The child tab is read-only. A direct subagent wire path is required to change this.

Classified as an agent limit: in the Claude Code 2.1.289 bundle the user message schema has no field that identifies a subagent, and the control requests include stop_task but no request that sends a message to a task. The Remote Control bridge in the bundle ignores an inbound user frame that has a parent_tool_use_id, as an echo of a subagent frame. The headless documentation (checked 2026-10-05) uses parent_tool_use_id only to mark subagent output. The terminal app reaches a subagent through its own in-process path.

codex.userNote: Codex rejects direct input to a subagent that Multi-Agent V2 starts, so the child tab is read-only. Upstream tracks this in [openai/codex#33885](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/33885).
codex.detailNote:
Codex Multi-Agent V2 rejects direct app-server input for spawned child threads. LeapMux keeps their transcripts read-only. See providers/codex/provider.go.

Classified as an agent limit: Codex Multi-Agent V2 child threads are read-only. Both turn/start and turn/steer answer "direct app-server input is not allowed for multi-agent v2 sub-agents". Upstream issues 33885 and 34377 ask for direct input and are open (checked 2026-10-05).

Tested version: Codex 0.160.0.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/33885> (open): Reports that MultiAgentV2 child threads are read-only and that app-server clients get "direct app-server input is not allowed for multi-agent v2 sub-agents".

cursor.userNote: Cursor announces each subagent with no input capability and takes no message for it. The subagent tab stays read-only while the subagent runs.
cursor.detailNote:
Cursor provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as an agent limit: Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 sends subagent_spawned with capabilities {} and accepts session/prompt for the parent session only (installed bundle read 2026-10-05).

github-copilot.userNote: Copilot can send a message to a background agent task, but LeapMux does not use that yet, so the child tab is read-only.
github-copilot.detailNote:
GitHub Copilot provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the Copilot 1.0.87 SDK has session.tasks.sendMessage ("Sends a message to a background agent task") and an agent task record that holds the tool call ID and the latest prompt. The built-in tool list has write_agent. LeapMux does not call any session.tasks method. The method targets a background agent task, so a foreground child can behave differently.

kilo.userNote: Kilo runs a subagent as its own session, and its server does not refuse a message for that session. LeapMux does not send one yet. The subagent tab stays read-only.
kilo.detailNote:
Kilo provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with low confidence: Kilo 7.8.1 keeps the OpenCode route session.prompt_async, which takes any session ID. Kilo documents that a task child cannot ask the user directly, and no source check shows a refusal for a message to a child session. No live test ran, because agent runs are not allowed. The maintainers may prefer an agent limit.

opencode.userNote: OpenCode runs a subagent as its own session, and its server does not refuse a message for that session. OpenCode's own interface offers no input there, and LeapMux does not send one yet. The subagent tab stays read-only.
opencode.detailNote:
OpenCode provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with low confidence: the OpenCode 1.18.34 route session.prompt_async takes any session ID and the prompt code has no parent check that refuses a child session. The OpenCode terminal client hides its prompt in a child session (tui routes/session/index.tsx), so the maintainers may prefer an agent limit. No live test ran, because agent runs are not allowed.

goose.userNote: Goose runs a subagent inside a tool call and has no way to send it a message while it runs. The subagent tab stays read-only.
goose.detailNote:
Goose provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as an agent limit: Goose 1.53.0 runs a subagent as a delegate tool task with no session of its own on ACP, and the summon extension offers only the load and delegate tools (source read 2026-10-05).

pi.userNote: The `pi-subagents` extension routes a message to a running subagent only in the Pi terminal app. In other modes the text goes to the main model, so the child tab is read-only.
pi.detailNote:
Pi provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as an agent limit: the input handler of pi-subagents sets canDispatchDirectly only when ctx.mode is tui, and its comment states that steering and resuming are not available in headless modes. The steer_subagent tool is a model tool, not a client request.

Tested version: Pi 1.0.0.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix runs a subagent as a tool call and has no way to send it a message while it runs. The subagent tab stays read-only.
reasonix.detailNote:
Reasonix provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as an agent limit: no Reasonix 1.38.7 ACP request addresses a child run (source read 2026-10-05).

zcode.userNote: ZCode 3.14.4 refuses input to a subagent session, because it treats that session as read-only. [An open upstream request](https://github.com/zai-org/feedback/issues/659) asks for messages to active subagents.
zcode.detailNote:
ZCode provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as an agent limit: both session/send and the v4 command admission in ZCode 3.14.4 throw 'Subagent sessions are read-only' (reasonCode guard.subagentReadOnly) for a session of type subagent_child (zcode.cjs, checked 2026-10-05). Upstream issue zai-org/feedback#659 (open) asks for dynamic sub-agent steering.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/zai-org/feedback/issues/659> (open): A feature request for mid-task message queuing and real-time messages from the main agent to active sub-agents.

codewhale.userNote: CodeWhale's runtime has no route that sends a message to a running subagent. Only the model can message a subagent, so the subagent tab is read-only.
codewhale.detailNote:
The child transcript exists, but the current provider bridge exposes no direct input route for that child. Its composer is read-only.

Classified as an agent limit: in CodeWhale 0.10.0 the actions `message` and `followup` belong to the model-facing `agent` tool, and the HTTP API serves only `GET /v1/agent-runs` and `GET /v1/agent-runs/{id}` for runs (research and source checked 2026-10-05).

kimi-code.userNote: Kimi Code accepts a message that you type in the subagent tab while the subagent runs.
kimi-code.detailNote: Kimi Code accepts a typed message from its subagent tab while the child runs.

mimo-code.userNote: MiMo Code accepts a message typed in the subagent tab while the subagent runs.
mimo-code.detailNote: MiMo Code accepts a typed message from its subagent tab while the child runs.

qwen-code.userNote: Qwen Code gives a client no way to send a message to a subagent. Only the parent model can do it, so the subagent tab stays read-only.
qwen-code.detailNote:
The child transcript exists, but the current provider bridge exposes no direct input route for that child. Its composer is read-only.

Classified as an agent limit: the extension methods of Qwen Code 0.24.7 for a client (qwen/control/session/*) list task cancel and workflow actions. They list no message route to a child. The send_message tool is for the model (checked 2026-10-05).

oh-my-pi.userNote: Oh My Pi 18.4.9 and later can send a message to a running subagent. LeapMux does not use that yet, so the child tab is read-only.
oh-my-pi.detailNote:
The child transcript exists, but the current provider bridge exposes no direct input route for that child. Its composer is read-only.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the Oh My Pi RPC documentation, the changelog (18.4.9, 2026-10-01) and the 18.6.0 binary have steer_subagent, which sends a message to a running subagent as its user. LeapMux does not send it.

grok-build.userNote: Grok Build accepts a message for a running subagent only when its `active_agent_messages` feature is on, and the feature is off by default. LeapMux does not use it yet, so the subagent tab is read-only. See the [Grok Build subagent guide](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/main/crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/16-subagents.md).
grok-build.detailNote:
The child transcript exists, but the current provider bridge exposes no direct input route for that child. Its composer is read-only.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with medium confidence: the Grok Build 1.0.45 source defines x.ai/subagent/message, which queues or steers literal text to an owned child. The docs describe the send_subagent_message tool as off by default (GROK_ACTIVE_AGENT_MESSAGES or the features table). Without the flag the method answers method_not_found. Reclassify as an agent limit if the maintainers count an off-by-default flag as not offered (checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/main/crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/16-subagents.md>: The guide says the send_subagent_message tool is off by default and is enabled with GROK_ACTIVE_AGENT_MESSAGES or the features table; the root session can send a follow-up to a subagent it owns.

kiro.userNote: Kiro offers no way to send a message to a running subagent, so the subagent tab is read-only.
kiro.detailNote:
The child transcript exists, but the current provider bridge exposes no direct input route for that child. Its composer is read-only.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: the research of KAS 0.66.8 records no child steering and no child cancel method; the subagent docs describe only monitoring with Ctrl+G (checked 2026-10-05).

amp.userNote: Amp accepts stream input only for the main thread. It exposes no handle for a subagent, so LeapMux cannot send a message to one.
amp.detailNote:
Amp exposes the remote Task call and final report without a child session handle. LeapMux cannot open or control that native child independently.

Classified as an agent limit: the stdin schema of Amp 0.0.1791074829 accepts `user` lines for the main thread, and the `Task` call carries no child session ID (installed bundle and E2E spec checked 2026-10-05).

cline.userNote: Cline's hub has no command for one running subagent, so LeapMux cannot send a message to a subagent. The subagent tab is read-only.
cline.detailNote:
The child transcript exists, but the current provider bridge exposes no direct input route for that child. Its composer is read-only.

Classified as an agent limit: Cline 3.0.68 runs a `spawn_agent` child inside the parent run, and the hub persists the child session only when the child ends; no hub command sends input to a running child (source and research checked 2026-10-05). Teammate messages exist only as agent tools.

codebuddy-code.userNote: CodeBuddy Code has no way to send input to a running child agent in stream-JSON mode, so the child tab is read-only.
codebuddy-code.detailNote:
Junie, Letta Code, and Qoder CLI state on the wire that a child takes no further input. CodeBuddy Code's stream-JSON path offers no child-directed input route. Their child tabs are read-only.

Classified as an agent limit: the control request handlers of CodeBuddy 2.160.0 (initialize, interrupt, steer, set_model, set_permission_mode, set_config, rewind, and others) hold no child-directed input. The steer handler rejects a session id that differs from the main session (binary check, 2026-10-05).

junie.userNote: Junie offers no way to send a message to a running subagent, so the subagent tab is read-only.
junie.detailNote:
Junie, Letta Code, and Qoder CLI state on the wire that a child takes no further input. CodeBuddy Code's stream-JSON path offers no child-directed input route. Their child tabs are read-only.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: the subagent classes of Junie 26.9.22 define spawned, state-update, and child-event messages only. They define no send, cancel, or steer method for a child. A report says the wire marks a child as taking no further input; the spec shows the Worker refusing child input (checked 2026-10-05).

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code has no way to send a message to a running subagent, so its subagent tabs are read-only.
letta-code.detailNote:
Junie, Letta Code, and Qoder CLI state on the wire that a child takes no further input. CodeBuddy Code's stream-JSON path offers no child-directed input route. Their child tabs are read-only.

Classified as an agent limit: Letta Code 0.34.2 has no child-directed input command in its listener protocol (installed letta.js checked 2026-10-05).

dirac.userNote: Dirac subagents run inside the parent task and take no input from you, so the subagent tab is read-only.
dirac.detailNote:
Dirac child transcripts are read-only through this integration. The Worker rejects input to the real running child and sends none of that input to its native model request.

Classified as an agent limit. Dirac 0.5.17 runs each subagent in-process behind one use_subagents card. ACP session/prompt addresses only the parent session (source checked 2026-10-05).

qoder-cli.userNote: Qoder CLI runs a subagent as an isolated task that returns its result to the main session. It has no way to send a message to a running subagent, so its subagent tabs are read-only. See [Qoder subagents](https://docs.qoder.com/en/cli/subagent).
qoder-cli.detailNote:
Junie, Letta Code, and Qoder CLI state on the wire that a child takes no further input. CodeBuddy Code's stream-JSON path offers no child-directed input route. Their child tabs are read-only.

Classified as an agent limit: the Qoder CLI 1.1.65 control channel has no child-directed input request (installed binary strings and docs.qoder.com checked 2026-10-05). The documentation does not describe messages to a running subagent.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://docs.qoder.com/en/cli/subagent>: Describes a subagent as an isolated task that completes a subtask and returns its result to the main session. It describes no message route to a running subagent.

factory-droid.userNote: You can type in a Factory Droid subagent tab while the subagent runs. Droid sends the message to that subagent.
factory-droid.detailNote: Factory Droid accepts a typed message from its subagent tab while the child runs.

fast-agent.userNote: Fast Agent subagents take no input after they start, so the subagent tab is read-only.
fast-agent.detailNote:
Fast Agent child transcripts are read-only through this integration. The Worker rejects input to the real running child and sends none of that input to its native model request.

Classified as an agent limit. Fast Agent 0.10.42 runs a subagent with one generate call on an isolated clone. ACP session/prompt addresses the parent session only (source checked 2026-10-05).

deepseek-harness.userNote: A message typed in the child tab goes to that child agent, which keeps its earlier answers.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-child-controls-probe: a real continuable child has its own live follow stream. Its completed first turn starts an exact parent report. Native subagents/prompt sends the next prompt to the same child; that request retains the old child answer. interruptByParent closes the second turn as aborted with cause user. The parent consumes the native stopped report. Six strict mock requests, two exact parent reports, zero unexpected requests. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI subagents take no input from you, so the subagent tab is read-only.
gemini-cli.detailNote:
Child JSONL is read-only. Installed ACP offers only root session/prompt and no addressable native child session control.

Classified as an agent limit. Gemini CLI 0.62.0 ACP offers session/prompt for a root session only. The child records are files with no session control (upstream docs checked 2026-10-05).

command-code.userNote: Command Code's JSON-RPC mode sends new input to the parent turn only. It has no route to a child agent, so the child tab is read-only.
command-code.detailNote:
Native RPC turn/steer addresses the parent turn. No RPC route accepts a child ID or child input.

Classified as an agent limit: the RPC method table of Command Code 1.74.1 has no child input method, and turn/steer takes no child ID (dist/cli.mjs, checked 2026-10-05).

muse-code.userNote: No model tool addresses a child session, and the fold child links no child agent, so no composer can reach a child.
muse-code.detailNote: No model tool addresses a child session, and the fold child links no child agent, so no composer can reach a child. The deciding evidence came from the binary itself: its exported MSP schema and a live muse serve probe under the local mock.

claude-code.userNote: The Interrupt control of a subagent tab stops that subagent. The parent session keeps running.
claude-code.detailNote:
The Interrupt control of a subagent tab is what `SupportsChildInterrupt` reports. Claude Code stops a child through its `stop_task` control request, on the CLI's own task id. A provider that reports no interrupt leaves the child tab without that control.

Claude Code 2.1.289 has the stop_task control request that stops one task by its task ID. The Agent SDK reference (checked 2026-10-05) lists stopTask(taskId).

cursor.userNote: Cursor stops only the parent turn. It has no request to stop one subagent, so the subagent tab has no Interrupt control.
cursor.detailNote:
Cursor provides no independent child interruption route in LeapMux. Its child tab has no Interrupt control while the parent retains its own control.

Classified as an agent limit: the Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 ACP agent handles session/cancel for the parent session only, and announces each subagent with capabilities {} (installed bundle read 2026-10-05).

github-copilot.userNote: Copilot can cancel a background agent task, but LeapMux does not use that yet, so the child tab has no Interrupt control.
github-copilot.detailNote:
GitHub Copilot provides no independent child interruption route in LeapMux. Its child tab has no Interrupt control while the parent retains its own control.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the Copilot 1.0.87 SDK has session.tasks.cancel ("Cancels a background task") and session.cancelAllBackgroundAgents. LeapMux does not call any session.tasks method.

kilo.userNote: Kilo can stop one subagent session without stopping its parent, but LeapMux does not use that yet. The subagent tab has no Interrupt control.
kilo.detailNote:
Kilo provides no independent child interruption route in LeapMux. Its child tab has no Interrupt control while the parent retains its own control.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the Kilo 7.8.1 route session.abort takes the ID of any session, so it can stop a child session. LeapMux sends it for the parent only. No live test ran, because agent runs are not allowed.

opencode.userNote: OpenCode can stop one subagent session without stopping its parent, but LeapMux does not use that yet. The subagent tab has no Interrupt control.
opencode.detailNote:
OpenCode provides no independent child interruption route in LeapMux. Its child tab has no Interrupt control while the parent retains its own control.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the OpenCode 1.18.34 route session.abort takes the ID of any session, so it can stop a child session. LeapMux sends it for the parent only. No live test ran, because agent runs are not allowed.

goose.userNote: Goose can stop a background subagent only through a model tool call. It has no client request that stops one subagent, so the subagent tab has no Interrupt control.
goose.detailNote:
Goose provides no independent child interruption route in LeapMux. Its child tab has no Interrupt control while the parent retains its own control.

Classified as an agent limit: the only Goose 1.53.0 route to stop one subagent is the model tool call load with cancel true, and ACP has no child session to cancel (source read 2026-10-05).

pi.userNote: The `pi-subagents` extension offers no way to stop one subagent from outside the Pi terminal app, so the child tab has no Interrupt control.
pi.detailNote:
Pi provides no independent child interruption route in LeapMux. Its child tab has no Interrupt control while the parent retains its own control.

Classified as an agent limit: pi-subagents stops a subagent from its viewer, from the /agents menu, and through an event bus between extensions inside Pi. Its tools are Agent, get_subagent_result and steer_subagent, and none stops an agent. Pi RPC has no command for a child.

Tested version: Pi 1.0.0.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix has no request that stops one subagent. Cancel stops the whole turn, so the subagent tab has no Interrupt control.
reasonix.detailNote:
Reasonix provides no independent child interruption route in LeapMux. Its child tab has no Interrupt control while the parent retains its own control.

Classified as an agent limit: the only cancel in the Reasonix 1.38.7 ACP code is session/cancel for a whole session (source read 2026-10-05).

zcode.userNote: ZCode can cancel a background subagent without stopping its parent, but LeapMux does not use that yet. The subagent tab has no Interrupt control.
zcode.detailNote:
ZCode provides no independent child interruption route in LeapMux. Its child tab has no Interrupt control while the parent retains its own control.

Classified as a LeapMux limit (medium confidence): ZCode 3.14.4 serves session/cancelBackgroundTask, which stops a background task by ID, and its runtime stops a local agent task through the subagent port (stopLocalAgentBackgroundTask in zcode.cjs). LeapMux does not call the method. A foreground subagent has no separate stop. No live test ran, because agent runs are not allowed.

codewhale.userNote: CodeWhale 0.10.0 has no route that stops one subagent, so LeapMux cannot interrupt a subagent alone. A later CodeWhale release adds a cancel route for subagent runs.
codewhale.detailNote:
The current provider bridge exposes no native child interrupt route. LeapMux keeps the child Interrupt control absent and refuses direct child interruption.

Classified as an agent limit for the tested version 0.10.0: the installed binary holds no `POST /v1/agent-runs/{run_id}/cancel` route. The 0.10.1 source adds `cancel_agent_run`. After an upgrade this cell likely becomes a LeapMux limit. Recheck it then (binary and source checked 2026-10-05).

mimo-code.userNote: MiMo Code runs a subagent as an actor inside the parent's session and offers no request that stops one actor. Only the parent agent's own `actor cancel` call does, so the subagent tab has no Interrupt control.
mimo-code.detailNote:
The current provider bridge exposes no native child interrupt route. LeapMux keeps the child Interrupt control absent and refuses direct child interruption.

Classified as an agent limit: MiMo Code serves GET /session/{id}/actors to list actors and POST /session/{id}/abort for the whole session. It has no per-actor cancel route (route search of the server code, 2026-10-05). The actor cancel action exists as a model tool only. The check used source revision 698f0f2, which is later than 0.1.15.

oh-my-pi.userNote: Oh My Pi 18.4.9 and later can stop one running subagent without stopping its parent. LeapMux does not use that yet, so the child tab has no Interrupt control.
oh-my-pi.detailNote:
LeapMux keeps the child Interrupt control absent and refuses direct child interruption.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the Oh My Pi RPC documentation, the changelog (18.4.9, 2026-10-01) and the 18.6.0 binary have cancel_subagent, which aborts one subagent without aborting the parent turn. LeapMux does not send it. cancel_subagent is the native child interrupt route of the provider bridge.

kiro.userNote: Kiro offers no way to stop one subagent without its parent, so the subagent tab has no Interrupt control.
kiro.detailNote:
The current provider bridge exposes no native child interrupt route. LeapMux keeps the child Interrupt control absent and refuses direct child interruption.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: the research of KAS 0.66.8 records no child cancel method, and deleting the session aborts its children. The subagent docs describe no interrupt (checked 2026-10-05).

amp.userNote: Amp can stop only a whole run, not one subagent. It exposes no handle for a subagent, so LeapMux cannot interrupt one alone.
amp.detailNote:
Amp exposes the remote Task call and final report without a child session handle. LeapMux cannot open or control that native child independently.

Classified as an agent limit: Amp 0.0.1791074829 cancels through SIGINT or SIGTERM, which ends the CLI process and the whole turn, and the stream carries no child handle (research and interrupt probes checked 2026-10-05).

cline.userNote: Cline's hub can stop only a whole run, not one subagent, so LeapMux cannot interrupt a subagent alone.
cline.detailNote:
The current provider bridge exposes no native child interrupt route. LeapMux keeps the child Interrupt control absent and refuses direct child interruption.

Classified as an agent limit: `run.abort` of Cline 3.0.68 takes a session and stops the lead and its children; `team_cancel_run` is an agent tool, not a client command (source and research checked 2026-10-05).

codebuddy-code.userNote: CodeBuddy Code can interrupt only the whole session in stream-JSON mode, not one child agent. LeapMux refuses an interrupt from a child tab.
codebuddy-code.detailNote:
CodeBuddy Code exposes no child-specific interrupt operation through the protocol that LeapMux uses. The Worker rejects a child interrupt while the real child remains running and its parent still accepts interruption.

Classified as an agent limit: the interrupt handler of CodeBuddy 2.160.0 takes a session id and a reason. It aborts the session run and stops team members. It takes no child id and no task id (binary check, 2026-10-05).

junie.userNote: Junie offers no way to stop one subagent without its parent, so the subagent tab has no Interrupt control.
junie.detailNote:
Junie exposes no child-specific interrupt operation through the protocol that LeapMux uses. The Worker rejects a child interrupt while the real child remains running and its parent still accepts interruption.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: the subagent classes of Junie 26.9.22 define no cancel or interrupt message for a child. The spec shows the Worker rejecting a child interrupt while the child keeps running (checked 2026-10-05).

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code has no command that stops one subagent while its parent keeps running. You can interrupt only the parent agent.
letta-code.detailNote:
Letta Code exposes no child-specific interrupt operation through the protocol that LeapMux uses. The Worker rejects a child interrupt while the real child remains running and its parent still accepts interruption.

Classified as an agent limit: Letta Code 0.34.2 has no protocol command that stops one subagent (installed letta.js checked 2026-10-05).

dirac.userNote: Dirac cannot stop one subagent alone, so the subagent tab offers no Interrupt.
dirac.detailNote:
Dirac exposes no child-specific interrupt operation through the protocol that LeapMux uses. The Worker rejects a child interrupt while the real child remains running and its parent still accepts interruption.

Classified as an agent limit. Dirac 0.5.17 passes the abort signal of the parent task to each subagent run. ACP session/cancel addresses the parent session only (source checked 2026-10-05).

qoder-cli.userNote: Qoder CLI can stop a running subagent task by its task ID. LeapMux does not use that yet, so a subagent tab has no Interrupt control. See [Qoder subagents](https://docs.qoder.com/en/cli/subagent).
qoder-cli.detailNote:
The Worker rejects a child interrupt while the real child remains running and its parent still accepts interruption.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: Qoder CLI 1.1.65 handles stop_task for a local_agent task (installed binary strings checked 2026-10-05), and the root stream reports the task ID in task_started. stop_task stops one local_agent task, so Qoder does expose a child-specific interrupt operation in this version. A foreground child may not stop the same way, so a native run must confirm it.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://docs.qoder.com/en/cli/subagent>: A user can stop a running background subagent from the task list (/tasks) while it still runs.

factory-droid.userNote: Factory Droid has no command that stops one subagent while its parent keeps running. You can interrupt only the parent agent.
factory-droid.detailNote:
Factory Droid exposes no child-specific interrupt operation through the protocol that LeapMux uses. The Worker rejects a child interrupt while the real child remains running and its parent still accepts interruption.

Classified as an agent limit: droid.interrupt_session of Droid 0.233.0 takes empty params and stops the loaded session. The TaskStop tool belongs to the model (installed binary strings checked 2026-10-05).

fast-agent.userNote: Fast Agent cannot stop one subagent alone, so the subagent tab offers no Interrupt.
fast-agent.detailNote:
Fast Agent exposes no child-specific interrupt operation through the protocol that LeapMux uses. The Worker rejects a child interrupt while the real child remains running and its parent still accepts interruption.

Classified as an agent limit. The /subagents command of Fast Agent 0.10.42 accepts list, status, on, off, toggle and help. ACP session/cancel addresses the parent session (source checked 2026-10-05).

deepseek-harness.userNote: Interrupt in the child tab stops that child. The parent receives a report that the child stopped, and the parent keeps running.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-child-controls-probe: a real continuable child has its own live follow stream. Its completed first turn starts an exact parent report. Native subagents/prompt sends the next prompt to the same child; that request retains the old child answer. interruptByParent closes the second turn as aborted with cause user. The parent consumes the native stopped report. Six strict mock requests, two exact parent reports, zero unexpected requests. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI cannot stop one subagent alone, so the subagent tab offers no Interrupt.
gemini-cli.detailNote:
Installed ACP cancel addresses an active ACP session. Native child UUIDs are file identities and provide no child cancellation route.

Classified as an agent limit. Gemini CLI 0.62.0 ACP cancel addresses an active session. The child UUIDs are file identities with no cancel route (upstream docs checked 2026-10-05).

command-code.userNote: Command Code's JSON-RPC mode has no way to stop one child agent. The model can stop a child with its own tool call, but the child tab cannot.
command-code.detailNote:
The native agent_output tool can kill a child. Native RPC has no child cancel route, so the child tab cannot independently issue that tool call.

Classified as an agent limit: the native agent_output tool can kill a child, and the RPC method table of Command Code 1.74.1 has no child cancel method (checked 2026-10-05).

muse-code.userNote: No model tool cancels one child, and the fold child links no child agent, so no per-child Interrupt control exists.
muse-code.detailNote: No model tool cancels one child, and the fold child links no child agent, so no per-child Interrupt control exists. The deciding evidence came from the binary itself: its exported MSP schema and a live muse serve probe under the local mock.

cursor.userNote: Cursor steers a running turn in its own terminal interface, as [its documentation](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview) describes. Cursor 2026.09.28 has no steer request on the connection that LeapMux uses. LeapMux holds new input until the turn ends.
cursor.detailNote:
Cursor's protocol exposes no steer method. The installed Goose ACP handshake advertises no steer method, so LeapMux offers Preempt. Reasonix steers only when its CLI advertises a steer method. Qwen Code takes a steer at its next tool gap.

Classified as an agent limit: Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 handles a new ACP prompt by cancelling the pending one, and its ACP documentation lists no steer method. The Steering setting exists only in the interactive CLI (checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview>: The Cursor documentation says that in the CLI, pressing Enter while the agent works steers the active run at a safe boundary.

goose.userNote: Goose 1.53.0 has an unstable steer request ([issue](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/issues/10310)), but it does not advertise the request. LeapMux uses only steer requests that the agent advertises, so it holds new input until the turn ends.
goose.detailNote:
Cursor's protocol exposes no steer method. The installed Goose ACP handshake advertises no steer method, so LeapMux offers Preempt. Reasonix steers only when its CLI advertises a steer method. Qwen Code takes a steer at its next tool gap.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: Goose 1.53.0 implements on_steer_session for _goose/unstable/session/steer, but agent_capabilities_meta lists only recipeParameterScopes and localInference, so the LeapMux hook that reads agentCapabilities._meta.goose.sessionSteer.method never finds a method (source read 2026-10-05). A comment in the LeapMux Goose output code records a live probe that Goose accepted a steer and answered with queuedSteer. Whether LeapMux should use an unadvertised unstable request is a maintainer decision.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/issues/10310> (closed): The issue states that Goose implements the custom steer method _goose/unstable/session/steer and proposes the standard cancel-then-prompt flow instead.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix accepts guidance during a turn. LeapMux uses the steer request of Reasonix when the CLI advertises it, as Reasonix 1.38.7 does ([documentation](https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/blob/v1.38.7/docs/ACP.md)).
reasonix.detailNote:
Cursor's protocol exposes no steer method. The installed Goose ACP handshake advertises no steer method, so LeapMux offers Preempt. Reasonix steers only when its CLI advertises a steer method. Qwen Code takes a steer at its next tool gap.

Tested version: Reasonix 1.38.7.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/blob/v1.38.7/docs/ACP.md>: Reasonix 1.38.7 advertises the steer method _reasonix.io/session/steer under agentCapabilities._meta['reasonix.io'].sessionSteer.method and tells clients to read it from there.

zcode.userNote: ZCode 3.14.4 can add a message to a running turn (its `guide` delivery, described in [an upstream report](https://github.com/zai-org/feedback/issues/772)). LeapMux does not use that yet, so it queues the message for the next turn.
zcode.detailNote:
The installed ZCode app server has no `session/steer` method. Its `session/send` returns a busy error while a prompt runs, so LeapMux queues the message for the next turn instead of offering Steer.

Classified as a LeapMux limit (medium confidence): the ZCode 3.14.4 app server accepts the command v4/command sendText with requestedDelivery startNow, queue, or guide, and the engine emits turn.steerQueued and turn.steerDrained. LeapMux uses session/send, which fails with 'A prompt is already running for this session' while a turn runs. The v4 gateway is created for every app server, including stdio. No live test ran, because agent runs are not allowed.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/zai-org/feedback/issues/772> (open): A report that the Desktop queue button Steer stops the running turn, and that a real steering primitive, steerTurn with delivery guide, exists.

qwen-code.userNote: Qwen Code reads a steered message after the running tool batch ends. If the turn ends without another tool batch, LeapMux sends the message as the next prompt.
qwen-code.detailNote: Cursor's protocol exposes no steer method. The installed Goose ACP handshake advertises no steer method, so LeapMux offers Preempt. Reasonix steers only when its CLI advertises a steer method. Qwen Code takes a steer at its next tool gap.

codebuddy-code.userNote: CodeBuddy Code steers a running turn with text only. If the message attaches an image, a PDF, or another binary file, LeapMux sends the whole message as the next turn.
codebuddy-code.detailNote:
CodeBuddy Code accepts text while it works. Its stream-JSON steering path converts `control_request/steer.content_blocks` to text.

The steer handler of CodeBuddy 2.160.0 keeps the text of the content blocks only. SteerInput therefore refuses a non-text file, and the worker sends the whole input as the next turn. No image filename goes to the model as steer text. The image bytes reach the model in the next turn.

junie.userNote: Junie can take a steered message inside the running turn. [Junie describes it as steering the agent mid-task](https://junie.jetbrains.com/). LeapMux does not use that route yet. It sends the message as a prompt that Junie starts after the current turn.
junie.detailNote:
LeapMux steers by queueing a follow-up prompt, which starts the next turn rather than inserting into the running one.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with medium confidence: the Junie 26.9.22 jar defines SteeringMethod with the wire name _session/steering. Its SteeringRequest holds sessionId, prompt, and _meta. Its SteeringResponse outcome is injected or startedNewTurn. installSteeringHandler registers the method, and the initialize result sets _meta.steering.supported true. LeapMux SteerInput sends a plain session/prompt, which the spec shows starts the next turn. Junie therefore has a native steer method. Not tested live (checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://junie.jetbrains.com/>: The Junie home page lists 'Steer the agent mid-task. Change direction without starting over.' as a feature of Junie, in the section that covers the CLI and the IDE plugin.

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code 0.34.2 queues a message that arrives during a turn and runs it after the turn ends. It does not take new input into the running turn.
letta-code.detailNote:
LeapMux has no native mid-turn steering route for Letta Code on its App Server path.

Classified as an agent limit: Letta Code 0.34.2 queues input that arrives while a turn runs and starts a new run after turn_finished (native probe of 2026-10-05 and installed letta.js).

fast-agent.userNote: Fast Agent cannot take new input during a turn. LeapMux keeps your message queued and sends it as a new turn after the current turn ends.
fast-agent.detailNote:
Fast Agent does not accept a steering operation for the current native turn. The Worker keeps the input queued after its explicit refusal and delivers it in a later separate native turn.

Classified as an agent limit. Fast Agent 0.10.42 has no steering term in its source. Its ACP server runs one prompt task for each session (source checked 2026-10-05). The Worker keeps the input queued after its own refusal.

deepseek-harness.userNote: DeepSeek Harness adds new input to the running turn, and the next model request includes it.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-native-steer-probe uses existing createToolOutputControl. A real native Bash command writes its first filesystem/output signal and stays open. session/prompt mode=steer admits the new text into that active turn. The next model request contains that exact steering text and the actual command output. Two strict mock requests, one durable turn end, zero unexpected requests. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI cannot take new input during a turn in the mode that LeapMux uses: a second prompt cancels the running one. LeapMux keeps your message queued until the turn ends.
gemini-cli.detailNote:
The installed ACP initialize response advertises no steering route. A concurrent prompt aborts/replaces the pending prompt rather than steering its current turn.

Classified as an agent limit. Gemini CLI 0.62.0 has model steering only in its terminal interface. Its ACP code has no steering term (source checked 2026-10-05). The initialize response has no steer capability. A concurrent session/prompt aborts the pending prompt. The Worker offers Preempt and keeps the input queued.

command-code.userNote: Command Code takes new text for a running turn. If the message attaches an image, LeapMux sends the whole message as the next turn.
command-code.detailNote:
The native RPC dispatcher accepts turn/steer for an active turn and emits steers_delivered. LeapMux keeps the active turn and classifies a stopped turn separately from delivery failure.

SteerInput of LeapMux returns ErrSteeringUnsupported for a non-text attachment, so the worker queues the message as the next turn.

claude-code.userNote: Claude Code reports progress for each agent of a Workflow run, but LeapMux does not use it yet. The Background tasks sidebar shows the run as one row.
claude-code.detailNote:
ZCode sends a workflow task without group metadata. Codewhale and Qwen send one self-grouped workflow row but no separate child or stage row. One row does not group work.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the Claude Code 2.1.289 bundle emits task_progress frames with a workflow_progress list of workflow_phase and workflow_agent entries (index, state, label, phaseTitle), through the same emitter as task_started. LeapMux reads task_started, task_progress and task_notification, but it ignores workflow_progress. The CLI sends the per-agent progress, and LeapMux does not read it. No live capture exists, because no test uses a real model account, so this rests on the bundle.

codex.userNote: Codex has no workflow feature that groups work. Each exec call stays a separate tool call.
codex.detailNote:
Native Codex exec sequences remain separate tool calls. LeapMux creates no workflow registry group for those calls.

Classified as an agent limit: the Codex 0.160.0 thread items hold no workflow or group entry (agentMessage, commandExecution, fileChange, mcpToolCall, dynamicToolCall, collabAgentToolCall and others). Sequential exec calls report no group key.

cursor.userNote: Cursor reports each subagent alone, with no workflow group. The Background tasks sidebar cannot show subagents under one workflow heading.
cursor.detailNote:
Cursor reports native child tasks without workflow group keys on this LeapMux path. The Background tasks sidebar cannot place those children under a workflow heading.

Classified as an agent limit: the subagent frames of Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 carry no workflow or group key (installed bundle read 2026-10-05).

github-copilot.userNote: A Copilot extension can define a workflow (a factory) that starts subagents. Copilot tags each subagent with the run ID, but LeapMux does not use it yet, so the Background tasks sidebar does not group them.
github-copilot.detailNote:
GitHub Copilot reports native child tasks without workflow group keys on this LeapMux path. The Background tasks sidebar cannot place those children under a workflow heading.

Classified as a LeapMux limit, with low confidence: the Copilot 1.0.87 SDK documents Agent Factories as extension-authored, session-scoped workflows that coordinate subagents. The subagent.started event carries factoryRunId, and the runtime reports factory_completed notifications. LeapMux hides the factory. events as experiments and reads no factoryRunId. A plain task subagent has no factoryRunId, which matches the first paragraph. No factory is registered in the E2E setup, so no live capture exists.

kilo.userNote: Kilo 7.8.1 has no workflow feature. It reports subagent tasks without a group, so the Background tasks sidebar shows no workflow heading.
kilo.detailNote:
Kilo reports native child tasks without workflow group keys on this LeapMux path. The Background tasks sidebar cannot place those children under a workflow heading.

Classified as an agent limit: Kilo 7.8.1 has no workflow concept in its tools or events. It reports a task as a child session with a parent ID only. Kilo Swarm is a shared message board, not a workflow group (source search 2026-10-05).

opencode.userNote: OpenCode 1.18.34 has no workflow feature. It reports subagent tasks without a group, so the Background tasks sidebar shows no workflow heading.
opencode.detailNote:
OpenCode reports native child tasks without workflow group keys on this LeapMux path. The Background tasks sidebar cannot place those children under a workflow heading.

Classified as an agent limit: OpenCode 1.18.34 has no workflow concept in its tools or events. It reports a task as a child session with a parent ID only (source search 2026-10-05).

goose.userNote: Goose reports each subagent alone, with no workflow group. The Background tasks sidebar cannot show subagents under one workflow heading.
goose.detailNote:
Goose reports native child tasks without workflow group keys on this LeapMux path. The Background tasks sidebar cannot place those children under a workflow heading.

Classified as an agent limit: the Goose 1.53.0 delegate tool call and its notifications carry no workflow or group key (source read 2026-10-05).

pi.userNote: The `pi-subagents` extension starts a workflow run in the background and reports only a task ID. It sends no progress for the stages of the run, so the sidebar shows one task.
pi.detailNote:
Pi's SubagentWorkflow runs native child stages, but its RPC updates expose one task without workflow group keys or stage rows. LeapMux cannot show grouped workflow work.

Classified as an agent limit: the SubagentWorkflow tool of pi-subagents runs the workflow in the background and returns details with the task ID only. Its execute function ignores the update callback, and the extension keeps the agents of a run out of its own lists.

Tested version: Pi 1.0.0.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix reports each subagent alone, with no workflow group. The Background tasks sidebar cannot show subagents under one workflow heading.
reasonix.detailNote:
Reasonix reports native child tasks without workflow group keys on this LeapMux path. The Background tasks sidebar cannot place those children under a workflow heading.

Classified as an agent limit: the Reasonix 1.38.7 task and read_only_task tool calls carry no workflow or group key, and the ACP code has no group concept (source read 2026-10-05).

zcode.userNote: ZCode reports workflow runs and their steps through a command that LeapMux does not read yet. LeapMux sees one workflow task row only, so the sidebar shows no workflow heading.
zcode.detailNote:
Claude Code runs a Workflow child but sends LeapMux only the top-level workflow task row. ZCode sends a workflow task without group metadata. Codewhale and Qwen send one self-grouped workflow row but no separate child or stage row. One row does not group work.

Classified as a LeapMux limit (low confidence): ZCode 3.14.4 serves v4/conversation/workflowRuns, workflowRunEvents, and workflowRunNodeResult, which describe the nodes of a workflow run. The session events that LeapMux reads give one workflow task without group data. LeapMux calls none of the v4 methods. No live test ran, because agent runs are not allowed.

codewhale.userNote: CodeWhale reports a workflow as one item with a status. It sends no row for each child, so LeapMux shows one workflow row and has nothing to group under it.
codewhale.detailNote:
Claude Code runs a Workflow child but sends LeapMux only the top-level workflow task row. ZCode sends a workflow task without group metadata. Codewhale and Qwen send one self-grouped workflow row but no separate child or stage row. One row does not group work.

Classified as an agent limit: the `workflow` result metadata of CodeWhale 0.10.0 holds the run id, the status, and the terminal flag; the child `agent.*` events never reach a runtime thread, and no field ties a child to the workflow. The E2E spec shows two native units inside one opaque row. Medium confidence: the `/v1/agent-runs` records might link children to a workflow, and LeapMux does not read them for that (research and source checked 2026-10-05).

qwen-code.userNote: LeapMux shows a Qwen Code workflow as one row. Qwen Code reports the steps of a workflow only when a client asks for its task status, and LeapMux does not ask yet.
qwen-code.detailNote:
Claude Code runs a Workflow child but sends LeapMux only the top-level workflow task row. ZCode sends a workflow task without group metadata. Codewhale and Qwen send one self-grouped workflow row but no separate child or stage row. One row does not group work.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with medium confidence: qwen/status/session/tasks with includeWorkflows:true returns each workflow run with phaseVisits, currentPhase, and dispatches (label, status, subagentId) in Qwen Code 0.24.7. LeapMux calls the method only to find a subagent for interrupt and never asks for workflows. The streamed session updates carry one workflow tool call and no child rows. Not tested against a live Qwen Code (checked 2026-10-05).

oh-my-pi.userNote: Oh My Pi has no workflow feature that groups work. It reports each subagent as a separate task.
oh-my-pi.detailNote:
The native output provides no workflow group that contains at least two work rows.

Classified as an agent limit, with low confidence: Oh My Pi 18.6.0 has no workflow concept in its RPC protocol. Its subagent_lifecycle frames carry index and parentToolCallId, so the subagents that one task call starts share a parent call. That is a grouping that LeapMux could derive, and it is not a native workflow group. The maintainers can decide to treat it as one.

amp.userNote: Amp's stream has no workflow structure. Each subagent call appears as its own row, so LeapMux groups none of them.
amp.detailNote:
The stream also carries no child messages and no workflow activity.

Classified as an agent limit: Amp 0.0.1791074829 shows cross-thread tools (`create_thread`, `wait_for_threads`) and `Task` calls as ordinary tool calls with no group key (research checked 2026-10-05). The E2E spec shows two separate rows with no workflow heading.

junie.userNote: Junie reports each subagent as a separate row with no workflow grouping, so the Background tasks sidebar shows no workflow heading.
junie.detailNote:
Junie reports independent native child rows without workflow grouping metadata. Two real children retain separate completed/running states. Their loaded Worker registry contains no workflow row or group before or after reload.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: subagent_spawned and subagent_state_update of Junie 26.9.22 carry the child session id, name, task, and state, and no workflow or group field (checked 2026-10-05).

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code reports a workflow only as one background process with phase counts. It sends no separate row for each agent of a workflow, so LeapMux shows no workflow group.
letta-code.detailNote:
Letta Code's `Workflow` tool exists in the toolset but emits no workflow grouping events on the wire. A background process summary can carry `kind:"workflow"`, and LeapMux draws no group from it.

Classified as an agent limit with low confidence: the background process snapshot of Letta Code 0.34.2 holds per-phase counts for a workflow, not one row for each workflow agent (installed letta.js checked 2026-10-05). LeapMux could draw the phase counts as a group, so a LeapMux limit is possible.

dirac.userNote: Dirac reports each subagent on its own and sends no workflow group, so the sidebar lists the subagents as separate rows.
dirac.detailNote:
Dirac reports independent native child rows without workflow grouping metadata. Two real children retain separate completed/running states. Their loaded Worker registry contains no workflow row or group before or after reload.

Classified as an agent limit. The Dirac 0.5.17 child card input holds isSubagent, agentId, agentName, taskTitle and prompt. It has no group or workflow field (source checked 2026-10-05).

qoder-cli.userNote: Qoder sends the start of each workflow child task but no child messages while the workflow runs. LeapMux shows each child prompt while it runs. When the workflow ends, LeapMux loads each saved child transcript that Qoder keeps.
qoder-cli.detailNote: Qoder sends workflow child task starts but no child message frames on stream JSON. LeapMux shows each child prompt while it runs. When the workflow finishes, LeapMux loads each saved child transcript from Qoder's journal.

factory-droid.userNote: Factory Droid runs its multi-agent missions only through the one-shot `droid exec --mission` command. Droid refuses a mission on the streaming input that LeapMux uses, so no workflow group appears. See [Droid missions](https://docs.factory.com/missions/reference).
factory-droid.detailNote:
Missions (its multi-agent workflows) are a one-shot `exec` surface and are refused on the streaming input LeapMux drives, so no workflow grouping appears.

Classified as an agent limit: Droid 0.233.0 refuses --mission with stream-json and stream-jsonrpc input, and LeapMux drives stream-jsonrpc (installed binary strings checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://docs.factory.com/missions/reference>: Missions run non-interactively through droid exec --mission -f mission.md. The page does not mention streaming input formats.

fast-agent.userNote: Fast Agent reports each subagent on its own and sends no workflow group, so the sidebar lists the subagents as separate rows.
fast-agent.detailNote:
Fast Agent reports independent native child rows without workflow grouping metadata. Two real children retain separate completed/running states. Their loaded Worker registry contains no workflow row or group before or after reload.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. The Fast Agent 0.10.42 subagent tool call holds a message and a label, and no group field (source checked 2026-10-05). The router and parallel workflow agents use a separate telemetry that LeapMux does not start.

deepseek-harness.userNote: The Background tasks sidebar groups the child agents of one DeepSeek Harness workflow under one heading.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-workflow-probe: durable run and agent events carried exact run/child identities for two children. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84. The native process announces a one-shot child before it writes the descriptor, so the follow retries.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI sends no workflow group for its subagents, so the sidebar lists each subagent as a separate row.
gemini-cli.detailNote:
Native child records carry no workflow group identity. Each exact root-owned UUID remains an independent row.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. The native child records of Gemini CLI 0.62.0 carry a child UUID and the root session. They carry no group and no direct-parent link (E2E evidence checked 2026-10-05).

command-code.userNote: Command Code reports each child agent as a separate event and has no workflow identity. The Background tasks sidebar cannot group children under a workflow heading.
command-code.detailNote:
Native agent calls emit individual child events. No native workflow identity joins two registry rows.

Classified as an agent limit: the event catalog of Command Code 1.74.1 holds subagent events only, and no event carries a workflow or run identity (checked 2026-10-05).

muse-code.userNote: Children run inside the workflow item fold, keyed by childId with no session of their own; the Worker draws one grouped row per fold child.
muse-code.detailNote: Children run inside the workflow item fold, keyed by childId with no session of their own; the Worker draws one grouped row per fold child.

gemini-cli.detailNote: Native closed-session proof uses installed 0.62.0 and the strict local mock. A session closed and reopened inside the same UTC minute fails native session/load with -32603 (No previous sessions found), because 0.62.0 names its archive for the minute and appends to the original file; upstream fixed that collision in [upstream fix](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/29463) ([native session issue](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/28693)), first released in v0.63.0-preview.0; stable 0.62.0 does NOT carry the fix, so the browser spec reopens a session archived in an earlier minute. A session from an earlier minute loads, and the reopened tab restores the stored LeapMux transcript and serves the next model request with the original native context. Gemini also starts native history replay without awaiting completion ([history replay issue](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/28775)), so replayed text can trail the session/load reply; the worker consumes that idle replay for the current session instead of storing it beside the copied transcript, and a prompt never inherits text buffered before it started.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the CLI help of CodeBuddy 2.160.0 describes --include-partial-messages as raw incremental model messages in stream-json output. The writer emits stream_event frames with text and thinking deltas. LeapMux starts the process without the flag.

junie.detailNote: Junie holds the model response and sends no ACP frame while it streams, so no live token count exists. It streams the output of a running shell command in rawOutput.output, and the Junie provider reads it into the live byte counter.

letta-code.detailNote:
The indicator cannot report an advancing token or byte count on this path.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with low confidence: Letta Code 0.34.2 streams text deltas, and the Letta adapter reports no token or byte count for them. Tool output windows are not cumulative byte counts (installed letta.js and LeapMux source checked 2026-10-05). The Letta adapter does report the text tail of a running tool output (OutputTailProgress in the tool output code), but it reports no counter and nothing for model text.

dirac.detailNote: Dirac streams model text in chunks. It runs execute_command in its own process, sends no terminal/create and states the output once after exit, so no live byte count exists.

qoder-cli.detailNote:
The LeapMux provider adapter stores native output but publishes no live ReportProgress update. The indicator cannot report an advancing token or byte count on this path.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: Qoder CLI 1.1.65 sends stream_event frames with partial content, and the root adapter reports no token or byte count from them (LeapMux source checked 2026-10-05).

factory-droid.detailNote:
