Classified as a LeapMux limit with low confidence: Qoder CLI 1.1.65 supports output styles natively (init frame field and style loader). Which request selects a style in a running session was not verified. LeapMux offers no style option (installed binary strings checked 2026-10-05).

factory-droid.detailNote:
The current LeapMux native setting groups offer no separate output style setting. A model variant or native TUI/slash command does not satisfy this feature.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with low confidence: Droid 0.233.0 selects an output style through the outputStyle setting in the settings file that LeapMux writes at launch. The session protocol has no style field, so a change needs a restart (installed binary strings checked 2026-10-05).

fast-agent.detailNote:
The current LeapMux native setting groups offer no separate output style setting. A model variant or native TUI/slash command does not satisfy this feature.

Classified as an agent limit with low confidence. Fast Agent 0.10.42 reports no config option in its ACP session. It sets text verbosity only through its text command /model verbosity, which LeapMux does not drive (upstream source checked 2026-10-05). Text verbosity may not count as an output style.

codex.detailNote:
LeapMux exposes no separate output style control through this provider integration.

Classified as an agent limit: the Codex 0.160.0 personality parameter is deprecated. The README states that friendly and pragmatic no longer select a style and that model/list reports supportsPersonality false for every model.

deepseek-harness.detailNote:
The Remote session settings and LeapMux adapter expose no output-style selection. Model selection, effort, plan mode, and permissions remain the available setting axes. Installed release: 0.2.0-rc.2, source 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

Classified as an agent limit: the Remote session settings expose model, effort, plan mode, and permissions. The dsh-persona package sets a persona inside an agent preset composition, and that is configuration and not a session setting.

gemini-cli.detailNote:
No native ACP output style setting exists.

Classified as an agent limit. The ACP dispatcher of Gemini CLI 0.62.0 implements setSessionMode and unstable_setSessionModel only. The source has no response style setting (upstream docs and source checked 2026-10-05).

command-code.detailNote:
The CLI and RPC expose no native output-style setting.

Classified as an agent limit: a search of dist/cli.mjs in Command Code 1.74.1 finds no output-style option or setting (checked 2026-10-05).

muse-code.detailNote: The MSP surface exposes setModel, setReasoningEffort, and setApprovalMode alone; no response-style setting exists.

amp.userNote: Amp lists a `code_exec` tool that runs code that the model writes. Amp's documentation says that this tool calls MCP tools. No LeapMux test covers the tool yet. See [Amp's MCP documentation](https://ampcode.com/docs/customize/mcp).
amp.detailNote:
Amp has a server-side `code_exec` tool. The init tool list of a real Amp (version 0.0.1790208065, probe) holds `code_exec`, and the bundle of version 0.0.1791074829 says that every agent gets `code_exec`. The Amp documentation says that Amp discovers saved remote MCP tools with `tool_search` and calls them through `code_exec` ([Amp's MCP documentation](https://ampcode.com/docs/customize/mcp), fetched 2026-10-05).

LeapMux does not verify `code_exec`. The E2E spec reads only the local executor catalog (`amp tools list`), where a server-side tool never appears. Its regular expression does not match `code_exec`. The passing spec therefore shows that the local catalog holds no script executor, and it shows nothing about `code_exec`. The permission helper never asks about `code_exec`, because the tool is server-side. Runtime `node_repl` strings do not identify a callable tool.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with low confidence (checked 2026-10-05). Open question for the maintainers: replace the spec with one that checks the tool list of the real Amp init message.

claude-code.userNote: Claude Code runs JavaScript that the model writes as a dynamic workflow. The script starts subagents and cannot run commands or read files itself. On the Pro plan, turn on dynamic workflows in `/config`. See the [workflows documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows).
claude-code.detailNote:
Native `Workflow` executes JavaScript source that the model supplies. Its native completion returns computed values or script errors. Native task and run identifiers identify the execution. The originating tool call identifier remains available also. The unavailable builtin REPL does not prevent this workflow route.

The Claude Code workflows documentation (checked 2026-10-05) states that a workflow script is JavaScript that a runtime executes, that the script has no direct file or shell access, and that Pro plans turn workflows on in /config.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows>: Describes the dynamic workflow as a JavaScript script that a runtime executes. States that the script has no direct filesystem or shell access, and that Pro plans turn it on in /config.

cline.userNote: Cline has no tool that runs code that the model writes. Its tools cover shell commands, files, search, web access, questions, and agents.
cline.detailNote:
The current installed CLI lists its complete builtin metadata, including disabled capabilities and native team tools. Its active native turn and actual shell execution pass. This builtin inventory supplies no general script executor.

Classified as an agent limit: the complete builtin catalog of Cline 3.0.68 (read_files, search_codebase, run_commands, editor or apply_patch, fetch_web_content, skills, ask_question, spawn_agent, the team tools, web_search) holds no script executor; the E2E spec reads the catalog from the installed CLI (source and spec checked 2026-10-05).

codewhale.userNote: CodeWhale runs model-written code with its `js_execution` and `code_execution` tools. The model first activates them with `tool_search`, and your machine needs Node or Python for the matching interpreter. A script that `execute_tools` runs can call only read-only tools that need no approval.
codewhale.detailNote: Native js_execution, code_execution, execute_tools. Use native tool_search to activate deferred execution tools. Node or Python must exist for the respective interpreter. Installed execute_tools permits read-only, auto-approved native tools. It refuses MCP, writes, shell, workflows, and nested execution.

codex.userNote: Codex runs JavaScript that the model writes through its `exec` tool, and the script can call Codex tools. Codex truncates long script output and keeps the start and the end.
codex.detailNote: Codex supplies native exec with JavaScript and registered tool calls. It truncates large script output with a warning and preserves the head and tail. The native result reports no output file path.

cursor.userNote: Cursor 2026.09.28 has no tool that runs code that the model writes, apart from ordinary shell commands.
cursor.detailNote:
Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 declares 69 native ToolCall cases. The complete installed descriptor supplies shell, MCP, and desktop operations, with no general script executor.

Classified as an agent limit: the complete tool descriptor of Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 declares 69 ToolCall cases, and none is a code, script, or REPL executor (the E2E spec asserts this on the installed bundle, 2026-10-05).

dirac.userNote: Dirac runs model-written scripts through its command tool, which takes a script and a language. Node scripts use the interpreter of the host. A script cannot call other Dirac tools.
dirac.detailNote: Native execute_command accepts script and language fields. Node script execution uses the host interpreter through the native script wrapper. Scripts do not expose a nested agent-tool API. The complete installed registry confirms this path.

factory-droid.userNote: Factory Droid runs JavaScript that the model supplies through its Script and WaitForScript tools. These tools need the `script_tools` feature and the `direct_and_script` mode to be on. Each Script call starts a new evaluation, and a script can call Droid tools.
factory-droid.detailNote: Droid supplies native JavaScript Script and WaitForScript tools when the `script_tools` feature and `direct_and_script` mode are enabled. Each Script call starts a fresh evaluation. Scripts can call native tools. The isolated native test proves output, failure status, and reload retention.

fast-agent.userNote: The default tools of Fast Agent include a shell but no tool that runs model-written code in a chosen language.
fast-agent.detailNote:
Harness tools inspect commands and resources. Anthropic code_execution hits preserve hosted server-tool results. A plugin named hf-codemode is optional. It does not prove installed native execution support.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. The complete Fast Agent 0.10.42 tool catalog read in the E2E run has the shell and no source executor (checked 2026-10-05). An optional plugin called hf-codemode exists. It is not installed. A hosted Anthropic code execution tool needs that provider route.

github-copilot.userNote: Copilot CLI has no tool that runs model-written code. Its 15 built-in tools cover shell, files, web fetch and agents.
github-copilot.detailNote:
Copilot 1.0.87 native tools.list reports a complete 15-tool builtin catalog for default, GPT, and Claude model selections. It contains shell and file tools, with no general code executor.

Classified as an agent limit: the native tools.list of Copilot 1.0.87 returns 15 built-in tools (bash, read_bash, stop_bash, list_bash, glob, grep, create, edit, skill, view, web_fetch, task, read_agent, list_agents, write_agent), with the same list for the default, GPT and Claude model selections. None is a code executor.

goose.userNote: Needs Goose's Code Mode extension, which is off by default. The model then runs TypeScript code, and the code can call other Goose tools. Tested with Goose 1.52.0.
goose.detailNote: Goose 1.52.0 supplies execute_typescript through its native code_execution platform extension. Scripts define run() and can call registered extension tools.

grok-build.userNote: Grok Build has no plain code tool. It runs the Rhai script of a model through its `workflow` tool, and the script starts subagents. LeapMux shows the script result or the script error when the workflow ends.
grok-build.detailNote:
The model calls the tool `workflow`. The xai-workflow engine of Grok Build executes the Rhai source that the model supplies (the internal function is `run_workflow`). It returns computed values or script errors. Shell `code_execution_result` metadata alone does not count.

The research notes on Grok Build list the host functions `agent()`, `parallel()`, `phase()`, `complete()`, `budget()` and others, which start and order subagents (checked 2026-10-05). They do not state whether a script can call another agent tool directly.

junie.userNote: Junie 26.9.22 has no tool that runs a script. It offers a shell tool, file tools, and subagents.
junie.detailNote:
The inspected installed launcher and bundle metadata identify no general executor. The browser spec confirms that the actual model catalog holds no code-execution tool.

Classified as an agent limit: the model request of Junie 26.9.22 lists open, scroll, ask_user, glob_search, grep_search, bash, answer, search_replace, multi_edit, create, undo_edit, submit, spawn_subagent, and agent_skill_read_doc. The spec confirms that the catalog holds no code execution tool. Ordinary shell does not count (checked 2026-10-05).

kimi-code.userNote: Kimi Code has no tool that runs code that the model writes. Its tools cover shell commands, files, search, web access, questions, goals, and agents. See [Kimi Code's tools reference](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/reference/tools.html).
kimi-code.detailNote:
The complete native registry includes inactive registrations and the controlled echo MCP fixture. It supplies file, shell, goal, planning, scheduling, and child tools, with no builtin general script executor. The native test also proves actual shell execution.

Classified as an agent limit: the complete native registry of Kimi Code 2.1.1 (Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, ReadMediaFile, Bash, WebSearch, FetchURL, plan, to-do, goal, cron, task, and agent tools) holds no script executor; the E2E spec reads the registry from the installed CLI (documentation and spec checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/reference/tools.html>: The built-in tools reference lists Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, ReadMediaFile, Bash, WebSearch, FetchURL, plan, to-do, agent, question, task, and cron tools, and no code execution tool.

kiro.userNote: Kiro CLI 2.24.0 has shell, file, MCP, and subagent tools, but no tool that runs a script. Its `code` tool searches code and does not run it. See the [Kiro tool list](https://kiro.dev/docs/reference/built-in-tools/).
kiro.detailNote:
Kiro CLI 2.24.0 starts KAS 0.66.8 for this integration. Its complete active native registry contains shell, file, MCP, and workflow orchestration tools. Its code intelligence tool does not execute scripts. The isolated test checks the closed registry, actual MCP execution, and real shell output.

Classified as an agent limit: the closed active registry of KAS 0.66.8 (Kiro CLI 2.24.0) has shell, file, MCP, and workflow orchestration tools. The documented tool list has no script executor besides shell (checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://kiro.dev/docs/reference/built-in-tools/>: The built-in tool list (read, glob, grep, write, shell, aws, web_search, web_fetch, introspect, code, tool_search, delegate, report, knowledge, thinking, todo, goal, session, subagent) holds no script executor besides shell.

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code has no standalone code interpreter. Its `Workflow` tool runs JavaScript that starts subagents. No LeapMux test covers that tool yet.
letta-code.detailNote:
The installed built-in catalogs include shell execution and Workflow, but no standalone code interpreter. Server-side custom tools can execute Python. They are not the installed local coding-agent executor.

The Workflow tool of Letta Code 0.34.2 runs JavaScript that the model supplies, and the script starts subagents (installed letta.js checked 2026-10-05). Claude Code, Qoder CLI, ZCode and Grok Build have a script tool of the same kind, and their cells are supported. The browser spec of Letta Code checks the actual model catalog for a standalone interpreter only. It does not run Workflow, so LeapMux does not verify the tool. A source audit on 2026-10-02 found that the Workflow handler of the installed Letta Code rejects every script while the backend is local. A native Workflow result needs the API backend. The evidence does not say whether a Workflow script can call other agent tools.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with low confidence. Open question for the maintainers: replace the spec with one that checks the real tool list and runs a Workflow script.

oh-my-pi.userNote: Oh My Pi runs model-written Python or JavaScript through its `eval` tool, and code can call session tools with `tool.<name>(arguments)`. Each language keeps its own runtime between calls. Python needs a usable interpreter. See the [eval documentation](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/tools/eval.md).
oh-my-pi.detailNote:
The native eval tool runs code. `tool.<name>(arguments)` invokes session tools. Each language keeps a persistent kernel. The browser spec runs an output script and a script that throws through eval and retains both results after reload.

The Oh My Pi 18.6.0 eval documentation (checked 2026-10-05) states that one tool call runs one Python or JavaScript cell in a persistent runtime, that code calls tools with tool.<name>(args), and that both runtimes are on by default (Python needs a usable interpreter).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/tools/eval.md>: Describes eval: one Python or JavaScript cell in a persistent runtime. Code calls registered tools with tool.<name>(args).

opencode.userNote: Needs the `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE` setting. OpenCode offers its `execute` tool for running code only when that setting is on. A script can call the connected MCP tools.
opencode.detailNote:
The native execute tool runs code. The registry includes execute only when enabled through OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE. The browser spec sets it in the isolated Worker. The confined interpreter exposes connected MCP tools.

OpenCode 1.18.34 registers execute when OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE or OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL is set (effect/runtime-flags.ts). LeapMux does not set the variable outside the E2E worker.

kilo.userNote: Needs the `KILO_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE` variable or the `experimental.code_mode` setting. Kilo offers its `execute` tool for running code only then, and a restricted-network session can hide it. A script can call the connected MCP tools.
kilo.detailNote:
The native execute tool runs code. The registry includes execute only when enabled through KILO_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE or the native experimental.code_mode setting. The browser spec sets KILO_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE in the isolated Worker. The confined interpreter exposes connected MCP tools. Restricted-network sessions can suppress it.

Kilo 7.8.1 loads the code tool when KILO_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE or experimental.code_mode is set (kilocode/tool/code-mode.ts). The tool registry suppresses it in a restricted-network session (session/tools.ts).

mimo-code.userNote: MiMo Code runs code through its `exec` tool. The tool is on for GPT-style models, or when `MIMOCODE_ENABLE_EXEC_TOOL` is set. A script can call the permitted session tools with `tools.<name>(arguments)`.
mimo-code.detailNote:
Native exec runs code when `MIMOCODE_ENABLE_EXEC_TOOL` or the native GPT toolset enables it. The browser spec sets `MIMOCODE_ENABLE_EXEC_TOOL` in the isolated Worker. `tools.<name>(arguments)` and `ALL_TOOLS` expose permitted session tools.

MiMo Code registers the exec tool when the GPT toolset applies to the model or when MIMOCODE_ENABLE_EXEC_TOOL is set (tool/registry.ts, source revision 698f0f2).

pi.userNote: Pi runs JavaScript that the model writes through its `codemode` tool, in a sandbox. Scripts call Pi and MCP tools. Turn on the tool with `"defaultTools": ["+codemode"]` in the Pi settings. See the [codemode documentation](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md).
pi.detailNote:
Native codemode. Activate the built-in codemode tool. `--no-extensions` requires explicit `builtin:codemode`. `tools.<normalizedName>(arguments)` invokes registered native and MCP tools.

The Pi 1.0.0 codemode documentation (checked 2026-10-05) states that codemode runs a script in a QuickJS sandbox with no Node, file or network access, and that scripts reach the outside through tools. The CLI documentation turns the tool on through defaultTools.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md>: States that the codemode tool lets the model write a JavaScript script that calls the other tools of Pi, and points to the Enable codemode section.

qoder-cli.userNote: Qoder's `Workflow` tool runs JavaScript that the model supplies, and the script starts subagents. It returns the computed result or the script error.
qoder-cli.detailNote:
Native `Workflow` executes JavaScript source that the model supplies. Tests verify computed results and script errors through native workflow identities. Node runtime REPL strings alone do not establish an exposed executor.

The Qoder workflows documentation (https://docs.qoder.com/en/cli/workflows, fetched 2026-10-05) says that workflow scripts are plain JavaScript that the model supplies. They start subagents and run in the background. The evidence does not say whether a script can call other agent tools.

qwen-code.userNote: Needs the experimental `tools.codeModeOnly` setting in Qwen Code 0.24.7. Qwen Code then runs the JavaScript of the model in an isolated `exec` tool, and scripts can call the tools that the session permits.
qwen-code.detailNote: Qwen Code 0.24.7 exposes exec when tools.codeModeOnly is enabled. Scripts use text() or return values and can call permitted session tools.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix 1.38.7 has no tool that runs code that the model writes. It has shell, notebook editing, and file tools. Notebook editing does not run cells.
reasonix.detailNote:
The source built-in tools offer bash/pwsh and notebook editing, with no standalone interpreter. Notebook editing does not execute cells.

Classified as an agent limit: the Reasonix 1.38.7 built-in tool directory holds no code, script, or REPL executor, and notebookedit edits cells without running them (source read 2026-10-05). The source is the tag v1.38.7, and the installed Reasonix is also 1.38.7 (Homebrew Caskroom path), so the source and the installed version agree.

zcode.userNote: ZCode runs JavaScript through its workflow feature. The model writes a workflow script, ZCode runs it, and the model reads the result or the script error.
zcode.detailNote:
Native workflow creation executes JavaScript source that the model supplies. Its native workflow read returns computed results or script errors. The browser and computer-use `mcp__node_repl__js` remains restricted.

The evidence records no statement on whether a workflow script can call agent tools, so the user note says nothing about it.

codebuddy-code.userNote: CodeBuddy Code offers its JavaScript REPL only in Code Mode or with `CODEBUDDY_REPL_ENABLED=1`. Scripts that run in it can call session tools.
codebuddy-code.detailNote:
CodeBuddy supplies a native JavaScript REPL when Code Mode or `CODEBUDDY_REPL_ENABLED=1` enables it. Native ToolSearch loads its schema. DeferExecuteTool invokes it. Scripts can call session tools.

The REPL gate of CodeBuddy 2.160.0 reads CODEBUDDY_REPL_ENABLED (1 or true enables it, 0 or false disables it) and otherwise follows the agent mode. The E2E spec uses the native ptc agent mode.

deepseek-harness.userNote: DeepSeek Harness runs model-written JavaScript with its `run_code` tool, and those scripts can call registered tool functions. Scripts in the workflow tool cannot call agent tools.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: The stored web-code-probe executed JavaScript through native workflow and computed 42. Native run_code exposes registered tool functions. The workflow route supplies no tools binding. Stored probe: native version 0.2.0-rc.2 and source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI has a shell tool but no tool that runs model-written code in a chosen language.
gemini-cli.detailNote:
The native tool catalog exposes ordinary shell execution and no dedicated code/source executor. Server model codeExecution parts are not an enabled CLI executor.

Classified as an agent limit. The native tool catalog of Gemini CLI 0.62.0, read in the E2E run, has ordinary shell execution and no source executor. Code execution parts that a Google model can return are not an enabled CLI tool (checked 2026-10-05).

command-code.userNote: Command Code offers shell commands but no tool that runs model-written source code in a language runtime, so LeapMux shows no code execution.
command-code.detailNote:
The complete native attached and deferred catalogs supply shell commands. They supply no dedicated source-and-language executor. The native select: lookup is a fuzzy search that loads the closest tool, and none of the loaded tools is REPL, codemode, run_code or execute_code.

Classified as an agent limit: the complete native tool catalogs of Command Code 1.74.1 hold no REPL, codemode, run_code, or execute_code tool. The select: lookup of the catalog is a fuzzy search that loads the closest tool (E2E spec).

muse-code.userNote: The workflow tool runs deterministic JavaScript in the native host; children submit through submit_result.
muse-code.detailNote: The workflow tool runs deterministic JavaScript in the native host; children submit through submit_result.

amp.userNote: Amp returns the end of a large shell output inline and states how many lines it dropped. It reports no file that holds the full output, so LeapMux shows no output path.
amp.detailNote:
A native large-shell tool result retains its output inline. The result carries no native output pointer. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: the native shell result of Amp keeps a 50,000-character tail with a `truncation.prefixLinesOmitted` count and carries no output pointer. The E2E spec proves the exact tail and the absence of a path row (native probes of the Amp tail limit recorded in the feature plan, spec checked 2026-10-05).

Tested version: Amp 0.0.1791074829.

claude-code.userNote: Claude Code reports the path of the file that holds the full output of a long tool result. LeapMux shows the path before the preview and does not read the file.
claude-code.detailNote: user.tool_use_result.persistedOutputPath, or one exact persisted-output tool_result wrapper with Full output saved to. The extraction matches the pointer to its session_id and tool_use_id. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

cline.userNote: Cline keeps the start and the end of a long command output inline and cuts the middle. It reports no file that holds the full output, so LeapMux shows no output path.
cline.detailNote:
tool.finished.payload result retains the native run_commands head/tail. No filesystem output pointer exists on this selected native route. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: `truncateCommandOutput` of Cline 3.0.68 keeps 48,000 characters (head and tail) and inserts a notice that tells the model to refine the command; it writes no output file and states no path (source checked 2026-10-05).

codebuddy-code.userNote: CodeBuddy Code saves long tool output to a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path before the preview and does not read the file.
codebuddy-code.detailNote: user.message.content tool_result text contains the exact persisted-output wrapper and Full output saved to filesystem path. The extraction matches the wrapper to its session_id and tool_use_id. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

codewhale.userNote: When CodeWhale reports a file that holds a saved tool output, LeapMux shows its path before the original preview. LeapMux never reads that file.
codewhale.detailNote: item.completed.payload.item.metadata.spillover_path with tool_use_id and native descriptor scope. Bash detail also ends with the native Full output footer. artifact_id alone is insufficient. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

codex.userNote: Codex keeps command output in its result and saves no file for it, so LeapMux shows no output path. Upstream tracks [a request to save the full output](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49907).
codex.detailNote:
Native commandExecution retains aggregated output and omission counts. Its command/session IDs and command input paths are not output files. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: the Codex 0.160.0 commandExecution item has aggregatedOutput, processId, exitCode and durationMs, and no output file path. Only image generation reports a saved path. Upstream issue 49907 asks Codex to save the full output of a truncated exec cell to a file, and it is open (checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49907> (open): Asks Codex to save the full output of a truncated exec cell to a file and tell the model the path. The dropped middle is gone today.

command-code.userNote: Command Code reports the path of a saved full tool output. LeapMux shows the path before the preview and does not read the file.
command-code.detailNote: tool_completed.event.result text contains the exact full output saved to footer, followed by native read_file guidance. The extraction matches the footer to its toolCallId and the shell_command tool. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

github-copilot.userNote: Copilot reports the path of the file that holds the output of a shell command. LeapMux shows the path and does not read the file.
github-copilot.detailNote:
tool.execution_complete result.contents shell_exit.outputFilePath is an explicit native filesystem path. The extraction matches the path to its parent session and toolCallId. One shellId can serve more than one call, so the toolCallId, not the shellId, identifies the row. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

The native tool.execution_complete event holds shell_exit.outputFilePath. One shell ID can serve more than one call, so LeapMux matches a path by the tool call ID.

cursor.userNote: Cursor sends only the exit code and the output text of a shell command. It sends no path for saved output, so LeapMux shows the output text only.
cursor.detailNote:
The selected native shell reply contains complete inline output and no fullOutputPath. Native process/blob IDs are not filesystem paths. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: the Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 ACP agent forwards only exitCode, stdout, and stderr for a shell call and drops the native output_location field (installed bundle read 2026-10-05). The E2E mock never sets the native spill threshold, so the spec proves only the inline case. The local Cursor store may hold more than ACP sends.

deepseek-harness.userNote: DeepSeek Harness reports the path of saved output when a tool output spills to a file. LeapMux shows the path before the preview and does not read the file.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: Native bash stream and dropped-output notices expose stdout and stderr spill paths. The spill-policy, grep and glob notices expose local stored-result locators. A native (unavailable) or could not be saved notice supplies no path, and the extraction rejects URI locators and opaque IDs. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

dirac.userNote: When a Dirac command prints very long output, Dirac saves the full output to a file and states its path. LeapMux shows the path and the original preview. LeapMux does not read the file.
dirac.detailNote: ACP rawOutput.output ends with exactly one Full output saved to filesystem path under `dirac/large-output-<native id>.log`. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

factory-droid.userNote: Factory Droid saves the full output of a shell command to a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path with the result and keeps the original preview.
factory-droid.detailNote: Execute tool_result exposes Full command output saved to filesystem path under `droid-terminal-*/<native id>.log`. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

fast-agent.userNote: Fast Agent saves long command output to a file only when it runs commands itself. LeapMux lets Fast Agent use the LeapMux terminal instead, so Fast Agent states no file path.
fast-agent.detailNote:
The selected ACP client-terminal route exposes terminal IDs and retained inline output. A terminal ID is not a filesystem path. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as a LeapMux limit with low confidence. Fast Agent 0.10.42 retains complete truncated shell output in a private temporary file. It includes the path in the truncation notice, on its local shell runtime only (upstream source checked 2026-10-05). The docs say the ACP client terminal is the default route. On that route the output has a terminal ID and a byte limit, and no path. No run of the local shell route was done.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI can save large old tool output to a file and give its model the path. It does not send that path to LeapMux.
gemini-cli.detailNote:
Native tool-output masking exposes a filesystem path in subsequent model context. The selected ACP tool result and stored native record do not expose that pointer to this transcript hook. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. Gemini CLI 0.62.0 replaces a large tool output in its model history with a tool_output_masked block that states the saved file path (upstream source checked 2026-10-05). The ACP tool result and the stored session record that LeapMux reads do not carry that block.

goose.userNote: Goose saves long shell output to a file and reports the path, but only when Goose runs the command itself. LeapMux gives Goose a terminal for commands, so Goose reports no path.
goose.detailNote:
Selected native shell result preserves the retained native inline output. Current captured route supplies no filesystem output pointer. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as a LeapMux limit: the Goose 1.53.0 developer shell tool writes output above 2000 lines or 50000 bytes to a file and returns 'Full output saved to <path>', but acp_shell sends the command to the client terminal when the client advertises the terminal capability, and that route saves no file (source read 2026-10-05). The route that LeapMux selects decides the result. The E2E spec proves only the client terminal route.

grok-build.userNote: Grok Build reports the path of the log file that holds the output of a shell command. LeapMux shows that path before the output preview and does not open the file.
grok-build.detailNote: ACP rawOutput type Bash carries output_file as an explicit native path. The extraction accepts the path only for its own call and native session under `sessions/<session>/terminal/<call>.log`. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

junie.userNote: Junie reports the path of saved shell output in its session event log, not in the live tool update. LeapMux shows that path before the output preview and does not open the file.
junie.detailNote: Native SessionA2uxEvent TerminalBlockUpdatedEvent carries outputFile.relativePath. New execute ACP frame exposes no direct path. The extraction reads a pointer-only supplement for the exact native call and opens no output file. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

kilo.userNote: Kilo saves long tool output in a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path above the preview. It does not read the file, and Kilo controls how long the file stays.
kilo.detailNote: Native OpenCode-family ACP rawOutput.metadata.outputPath is a filesystem path. The Kilo plugin reads the path through its own hook, which shares the OpenCode-family extraction. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

kimi-code.userNote: When Kimi Code saves a long tool output to a file, it states the path in the tool result. LeapMux shows that path before the original preview and never reads the file.
kimi-code.detailNote: tool_result.output includes native output_path in either the exact complete-output header or per-line footer. The extraction binds the path to its call, agent, session, and the native path format. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

kiro.userNote: Kiro reports the path of a saved tool output file. LeapMux shows that path before the output preview and does not open the file.
kiro.detailNote: ACP _meta.kiro.outputTransformation kind offloaded carries absFilePath. This is a native filesystem path, not a tool ID. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code ends a long tool result with the path of a file that holds the full output. LeapMux shows the path with the result and keeps the original preview.
letta-code.detailNote: Canonical tool_return_message tool_return ends with Full output written to filesystem path. The extraction rejects progress and lifecycle frames and keeps every real late final return. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

mimo-code.userNote: MiMo Code saves long tool output in a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path above the preview and does not read the file.
mimo-code.detailNote: Native HTTP message.part.updated properties.part.state.metadata.outputPath is a filesystem path. The extraction matches the path to its part callID and sessionID. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

oh-my-pi.userNote: Oh My Pi identifies saved tool output with an artifact ID, not a file path, so LeapMux shows no output path.
oh-my-pi.detailNote:
Native result.details.meta.truncation.artifactId is a numeric ID, not a path. The artifact directory can be adopted; nonpersistent sessions keep in-memory artifacts. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: the native truncation metadata of Oh My Pi 18.6.0 holds artifactId, a numeric ID that the wire carries as a string, and artifact:// is a URI scheme. The artifact file name holds that ID and the tool type, and Oh My Pi reports no path for it. An opaque ID or URI does not supply a filesystem path.

opencode.userNote: OpenCode saves long tool output in a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path above the preview. It does not read the file, and OpenCode controls how long the file stays.
opencode.detailNote: Native ACP rawOutput.metadata.outputPath is a filesystem path under `tool-output/tool_<native id>`. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

pi.userNote: Pi reports the path of the file that holds the full output of a long tool result. LeapMux shows the path before the preview and does not read the file.
pi.detailNote:
Native tool_execution_end.result.details.fullOutputPath is an explicit filesystem path. MCP and codemode retain their own native inline content. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

The Pi native result carries details.fullOutputPath (rpc-commands.md documents fullOutputPath for a truncated bash output).

qoder-cli.userNote: Qoder reports the path of a file that holds a saved tool output. LeapMux shows the path with the result and keeps the original preview.
qoder-cli.detailNote: Native user.tool_use_result.persistedOutput.path is a filesystem path. The extraction matches the path to its session_id and the exact tool_result.tool_use_id. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix sends no path for saved output. It cuts the output that it sends over the connection that LeapMux uses to 8000 characters.
reasonix.detailNote:
Native stored bash tool record supplies complete inline content behind the ACP preview. No filesystem output pointer exists on this selected native route. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: Reasonix 1.38.7 clips each ACP tool result with a note and never saves long output to a file (source searched 2026-10-05). LeapMux restores the complete output from the Reasonix session store, which holds inline content.

zcode.userNote: ZCode saves long tool output in a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path above the preview and does not read the file.
zcode.detailNote: Native stored tool state.metadata.serialization.artifactPath is an explicit filesystem path. zcode-artifact URI alone is not a path. The extraction matches the path to its native session and call and the sanitized path segments. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

qwen-code.userNote: Qwen Code reports the path of saved shell output. LeapMux shows that path before the output preview and does not open the file.
qwen-code.detailNote: Native shell_result outputFiles supplies reported output file paths. Background shell results can report a native truncation footer. LeapMux checks the exact native call and its observed opener. It keeps the original preview and reads no native archive or output file.
